body.translated_text: Success! Homage to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>.

children.translated_text: 1 Dhp 1
<s>Dharmas</s> have mind as their forerunner, mind as their chief, and are mind-made;

children.text: manasā ca praduṣṭena bhāṣate vā karoti vā |
children.translated_text: if one speaks or acts with a corrupted mind,

children.text: tato naṃ dukham anneti cakram vā vahato padaṃ ||
children.translated_text: then suffering follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the draft-ox.
<s>Dharmas</s> have mind as their forerunner, mind as their chief, and are mind-made;

children.text: manasā hi praduṣṭena bhāṣate vā karoti vā |
children.translated_text: if one speaks or acts with a corrupted mind,

children.text: tatas taṃ duḥkham anveti cakraṃ vā vahato padam ||
children.translated_text: then suffering follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the draft-ox.
2 Dhp2
<s>Dharmas</s> have mind as their forerunner, mind as their chief, and are mind-made;

children.text: manasā ca prasannena bhāṣate vā karoti vā |
children.translated_text: if one speaks or acts with a clear mind,

children.text: tato naṃ sukham anneti cchāyā vā anapāyinī ||
children.translated_text: then happiness follows him, like a shadow that never departs.
<s>Dharmas</s> have mind as their forerunner, mind as their chief, and are mind-made;

children.text: manasā ca prasannena bhāṣate vā karoti vā |
children.translated_text: if one speaks or acts with a clear mind,

children.text: tatas taṃ sukham anveti cchāyā vā anugaminī ||
children.translated_text: then happiness follows him, like a shadow that accompanies one.
3 Dhp15

children.text: iha śocati precca śocati pāpakam[mo ubhaya]ttha śocati |
children.translated_text: Here he grieves, hereafter he grieves — the evil-doer grieves in both states;

children.text: so śocati so vihaṃnyati dṛṣṭā kammakileśam āttano ||
children.translated_text: he grieves, he is afflicted, having seen the defilement of his own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: iha śocati pretya śocati pāpakammā hi ubhayatra śocati |
children.translated_text: Here he grieves, hereafter he grieves — the evil-doer grieves in both states;

children.text: sa hi śocati sa praśocati dṛṣṭvā karma hi kliṣṭam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he grieves, he deeply grieves, having seen the impurity of his own <s>karma</s>.
4 Dhp16

children.text: iha nandati precca nandati katapuṃño ubhayattha nandati |
children.translated_text: Here he rejoices, hereafter he rejoices — the merit-maker rejoices in both states;
he rejoices, he is [glad], having seen the purity of his own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: iha nandati pretya nandati kṛtapuṇyo hy ubhayatra nandati |
children.translated_text: Here he rejoices, hereafter he rejoices — the merit-maker indeed rejoices in both states;

children.text: sa hi nandati sa pramodate dṛṣṭvā karma viśuddham ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he rejoices, he delights, having seen the purity of his own <s>karma</s>.
5 Dhp3

children.text: ākrośi maṃ avadhi maṃ ajini maṃ ahāsi me |
children.translated_text: "He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me" —

children.text: ye tāni upanahyanti veraṃ tesaṃ na śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: for those who harbor such thoughts, hatred is never appeased.

children.text: ākrośan mām avocan mām ajayan mām ajāpayet |
children.translated_text: "He abused me, he reviled me, he defeated me, he caused me loss" —

children.text: atra ye hy upanahyanti vairaṃ teṣāṃ na śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: for those who harbor such thoughts, enmity is never appeased.
6 Dhp4

children.text: ākro[ṣi maṃ] avadhi maṃ ajini maṃ ahāsi me |
children.translated_text: "He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me" —

children.text: ye tāni nopanahyanti veraṃ tesaṃ upaśamyati ||
children.translated_text: for those who do not harbor such thoughts, hatred is fully appeased.

children.text: ākrośan mām avocan mām ajayan mām ajāpayet |
children.translated_text: "He abused me, he reviled me, he defeated me, he caused me loss" —

children.text: atra ye nopanahyanti vairaṃ teṣāṃ praśāmyati ||
children.translated_text: for those who do not harbor such thoughts, enmity is fully appeased.
7 Dhp7
One who dwells contemplating the pleasant, with senses unrestrained,
not knowing moderation in food, lazy and of weak effort —

body.text:
taṃ ve prasahate māro vāto rukkhaṃ va dubbalaṃ |
Uv29:15
śubhānudarśinaṃ nityam idriyaiś cāpy asaṃvṛtaṃ |
bhojane cāpy amātrajñaṃ hīnaṃ jāgarikāsu ca |
taṃ vai prasahate rāgo vāto vṛkṣam ivābalaṃ |
body.translated_text:
him <s>Māra</s> overpowers, as the wind overpowers a weak tree.
Uv29:15
One who always contemplates the pleasant, with senses unrestrained,
not knowing moderation in food, and lax in wakefulness —
him <s>rāga</s> (passion) overpowers, as the wind overpowers a weak tree.

8 Dhp8
One who dwells contemplating the unpleasant, with senses well-restrained,

children.translated_text: knowing moderation in food, [...] of aroused effort —

children.text: taṃ ve na prasahate māro vāto śelaṃ va parvvataṃ ||
children.translated_text: him <s>Māra</s> does not overpower, as the wind does not move a rocky mountain.
One who always contemplates the unpleasant, with senses well-restrained,

children.text: bhojane cāpi mātrajñaṃ yuktaṃ jāgarikāsu ca |
children.translated_text: knowing moderation in food, and diligent in wakefulness —

children.text: taṃ na prasahate rāgo vātaḥ śailam iva sthiraṃ ||
children.translated_text: him <s>rāga</s> (passion) does not overpower, as the wind cannot move a firm rock.
9 Dhp328

children.text: sace labheyā nipakaṃ sapraṃñaṃ sāddhiṃcaraṃ sādhuvihāradhīraṃ |
children.translated_text: If one finds a prudent, wise companion, a steadfast one of good conduct,

children.text: adhibhūya sabbāṇi pariśrav[ ] careyā tenāttamano satīmā ||
children.translated_text: having overcome all dangers, one should walk with him, glad at heart and mindful.

children.text: sa cel labhed vai nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ loke caraṃ sādhu hi nityam eva |
children.translated_text: If one should find a prudent companion, one walking well in the world, always truly,

children.text: adhibhūya sarvāṇi parisravāṇi careta tenāptamanā smṛtātmā ||
children.translated_text: having overcome all dangers, one should walk with him, glad at heart and mindful.

children.text: na ce labheyā nipakaṃ sapraṃñaṃ sāddhiṃcaraṃ sādhuvihāradhīraṃ |
children.translated_text: If one does not find a prudent, wise companion, a steadfast one of good conduct,

children.text: rājā va rāṣṭaṃ vijitaṃ prahāya eko ccare mātaṃgāranne va nāgo ||
children.translated_text: like a king who has abandoned a conquered kingdom, one should wander alone, as an elephant in the <s>Mātaṅga</s> forest.

children.text: na cel labhet vai nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ loke ca raṃ sādhu hi nityam eva |
children.translated_text: If one should not find a prudent companion, one walking well in the world, always truly,

children.text: rājeva rāṣṭraṃ vipulaṃ prahāya ekaś caren na ca pāpāni kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: like a king who has abandoned a vast kingdom, one should wander alone and not commit evil deeds.

children.text: ekassa caritaṃ śreyo nāsti bāle bitīyatā |
children.translated_text: The solitary life is better; there is no companionship with a fool.

children.text: eko ccare na ca pāpāni kayirā appussuko mātaṃgāranne va nāgo ||
children.translated_text: One should wander alone and not commit evil deeds, with few concerns, as an elephant in the <s>Mātaṅga</s> forest.

children.text: ekasya caritaṃ śreyo na tu bālaḥ sahāyatā |
children.translated_text: The solitary life is better; a fool is not a good companion.

children.text: ekaś caren na ca pāpāni kuryād alpotsuko 'raṇyagatai va nāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should wander alone and not commit evil deeds, with few concerns, as an elephant gone to the forest.
Through desire, hatred, fear, and delusion, whoever transgresses the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: nīhīrate tassa yaśo kālapakkhe va candramā ||
children.translated_text: his glory wanes, as the moon in the dark fortnight.
Through desire, hatred, fear, and delusion, whoever does not transgress the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: āpūrate tassa yaśo śuklapakkhe va candaramā ||
children.translated_text: his glory waxes, as the moon in the bright fortnight.
14 Dhp21
Heedfulness is the path to the deathless; heedlessness is the path to death.

children.text: apramattā na mrīyanti ye pramattā yathā matā ||
children.translated_text: The heedful do not die; the heedless are as if already dead.
Uv4:1

children.text: apramādo hy amṛtapadaṃ pramādo matyunaḥ padam |
children.translated_text: Heedfulness is the path to the deathless; heedlessness is the path of death.

children.text: apramattā na mriyante ye pramattāḥ sadā mṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The heedful do not die; the heedless are always as dead.
15 Dhp22
Having understood this distinction regarding heedfulness, the wise
rejoice in heedfulness, delighting in the domain of the noble ones.
Uv4:2

children.text: etaṃ viśeṣatāṃ jñātvā hy apramādasya paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having understood this distinction of heedfulness, the wise one
should rejoice in heedfulness — the noble one's own domain, always.
16 Dhp23
Those who meditate, persevering, always of firm exertion —
those steadfast ones attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the supreme security from bondage.
Uv4:3
The heedful, persevering, always of firm exertion —
those steadfast ones attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the supreme security from bondage.
17 Dhp26
The foolish, the unwise, devote themselves to heedlessness;

children.text: apramādan tu medhāvī dhanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ va rakkhati ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one guards heedfulness as the greatest treasure.
The foolish, the unwise, follow after heedlessness;

children.text: apramādaṃ tu medhāvī dhanaṃ śreṣṭhīva rakṣati ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one guards heedfulness as a rich man guards his wealth.
18 Dhp29
Heedful among the heedless, wakeful among the sleeping,

children.text: abalāṣṣam va śīghrāśśo hettā yāti sumedhaso ||
children.translated_text: the wise one advances, as a swift horse leaves behind a weak one.
Heedful among the heedless, wakeful among the sleeping,

children.text: abalāśva iva bhadrāśvaṃ hitvā yāti sumedhasam ||
children.translated_text: the wise one advances, as a swift horse leaves behind a weak one.
19 Dhp28
When the wise one drives away heedlessness with heedfulness,
having ascended the palace of wisdom, free from sorrow, he looks upon the sorrowing people,

children.text: parvvataṭṭho va bhoma 'ṭṭhe dhīro bāle avecchati ||
children.translated_text: as one standing on a mountain looks down upon those on the plain — the steadfast one upon the fools.
Uv4:4
When the wise one drives away heedlessness with heedfulness,

children.text: prajñāprāsādam āruhya tv aśokaḥ śokinīṃ prajām |
children.translated_text: having ascended the palace of wisdom, free from sorrow, he looks upon the sorrowing people,
as one standing on a mountain looks upon those on the ground — the steadfast one upon the fools.

children.text: pūrvve cāpi pramajjittā yo pacchā na pramajjati |
children.translated_text: One who was formerly heedless but afterwards is not heedless,

children.text: so imaṃ lokaṃ prabhāseti abhramutto va candramā ||
children.translated_text: he illuminates this world, as the moon freed from clouds.

children.text: yas tu pūrvaṃ pramādyeha paścād vai na pramādyate |
children.translated_text: One who was formerly heedless here but afterwards is not heedless,

children.text: sa imaṃ bhāsate lokam abhramuktaiva candramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he illuminates this world, as the moon freed from clouds.

children.text: pūrvve cāpi pramajjittā yo pacchā na pramajjati |
children.translated_text: One who was formerly heedless but afterwards is not heedless,

children.text: so imāṃ visattikāṃ loke sato samativattati ||
children.translated_text: he, being mindful, overcomes this attachment in the world.

children.text: yas tu pūrvaṃ pramādyeha paścād vai na pramādyate |
children.translated_text: One who was formerly heedless here but afterwards is not heedless,

children.text: sa imāṃ viṣaktikāṃ loke smṛtaḥ samativartate ||
children.translated_text: he, being mindful, overcomes this attachment in the world.
22 Dhp32
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who delights in heedfulness, who sees danger in heedlessness,
is incapable of falling away — he is in the very presence of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who delights in heedfulness, who sees danger in heedlessness,
is incapable of falling away — he is in the very presence of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text:
23 Dhp31
apramādagaru bhikkhū pramāde bhayadaṃśino
saṃyojanam aṇutthūlaṃ daham aggīva gacchati |
Uv4:29
apramādarato bhikṣuḥ pramāde bhayadarśakaḥ |
saṃyojanam aṇusthūlaṃ dahann agnir iva gacchati |
body.translated_text:
23 Dhp31
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who delights in heedfulness, who sees danger in heedlessness,
burns away fetters, both small and great, advancing like fire.
Uv4:29
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who delights in heedfulness, who sees danger in heedlessness,
burns away fetters, both small and great, advancing like fire.

body.text:
24 Dhp327
apramādaratā hotha saṃ cittam anurakkhatha ||
body.translated_text:
24 Dhp327
Delight in heedfulness! Guard your own mind well!

body.text:
duggā uddharathāttānaṃ pake sanno va kuñjaro |
Uv4:36/4:27
apramādaratā bhavata svacittam anurakṣata ||
body.translated_text:
Pull yourself out of difficulty, as an elephant sunk in mud.
Uv4:36/4:27
Be devoted to heedfulness! Guard your own mind well!

body.text: durgād uddharate tmānaṃ paṅkasan naiva kuñjaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Pull yourself out of difficulty, as an elephant from the mud.

25
Those who rejoice in heedfulness, prudent and restrained in virtue,

body.text: te ve kāle prācchanti yattha prātto na śocati |
body.translated_text: they indeed realize in due time that state where, having attained it, one does not grieve.

26
Rejoice in heedfulness, not in the flooding of sense-pleasures!

children.translated_text: Thus living, ardent, with a calm and unagitated mind,
devoted to mental tranquility, one may become a maker of an end of suffering.
27 Dhp24

children.text: uṭṭheyā na pramajjeyā dhammaṃ sucaritaṃ care |
children.translated_text: One should arise! One should not be heedless! One should practice the <s>Dharma</s> of good conduct!

children.text: dhammacārī [ ] śeti aśśiṃ loke paramhi ca ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner of <s>Dharma</s> sleeps happily in this world and in the next.

children.text: uttiṣṭhen na pramādyeta dharmaṃ sucaritaṃ caret |
children.translated_text: One should arise! One should not be heedless! One should practice the <s>Dharma</s> of good conduct!

children.text: dharmacārī sukhaṃ śete hy asmiṃ loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner of <s>Dharma</s> sleeps happily in this world and in the next.
28 Dhp24
For one who is energetic, mindful, of pure deeds, and acts with consideration,

children.text: saṃyyatassa ca dhammajīvino apramattassa yaśo 'ssa vaddhati ||
children.translated_text: who is restrained and lives by the <s>Dharma</s>, who is heedful — his glory increases.
Uv4:6
For one who is energetic, mindful, of pure mind, and acts with consideration,

children.text: saṃyatasya hi dharmajīvino hy apramattasya yaśo 'bhivardhate ||
children.translated_text: who is restrained and lives by the <s>Dharma</s>, who is heedful — his glory increases.
29 Dhp25
By effort, by heedfulness, by restraint and self-control,

children.text: dīpaṃ kayirātha medhāvī yam ogho nādhipūrati ||
children.translated_text: let the wise one make an island that no flood can overwhelm.
Uv4:5
By effort, by heedfulness, by restraint and self-control,

children.text: dvīpaṃ karoti medhāvī tam ogho nābhimardati ||
children.translated_text: the wise one makes an island that no flood can crush.

children.text: uṭṭhāṇakālamhi anuṭṭhihāno yuvā balī ālasiko upako |
children.translated_text: One who does not rise when it is time to rise, who though young and strong is lazy and idle,

children.text: saṃsannasaṃkappamano kusīdo praṃñāya māggaṃ alaso na yeti ||
children.translated_text: whose mind is full of collapsed intentions, the indolent one — that lazy person does not find the path of wisdom.

children.text: utthānakāleṣu nihīnavīryo vācā balī tv ālasiko nirāśaḥ |
children.translated_text: One of weak effort when it is time to rise, strong in words but lazy and without hope,

children.text: sadaiva saṃkalpahataḥ kusīdo jñānasya mārgaṃ satataṃ na vetti ||
children.translated_text: always struck down by his own intentions, the indolent one never finds the path of knowledge.

children.text: hīnaṃ dhammaṃ na seveyā pramādena na samvase |
children.translated_text: One should not follow a base <s>dharma</s>; one should not dwell in heedlessness;

children.text: micchadṛṣṭiṃ na seveyā na siyā lokavaddhano ||
children.translated_text: one should not follow wrong views; one should not be a perpetuator of the world.
Uv4:8

children.text: hīnāṃ dharmaṃ na seveta pramādena na saṃvaset |
children.translated_text: One should not follow a base <s>dharma</s>; one should not dwell with heedlessness;

children.text: mityādṛṣṭiṃ na roceta na bhavel lokavardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should not delight in wrong views; one should not be a perpetuator of the world.

children.text: na tāvatā dhammadharo yāvatā bahu bhāṣati |
children.translated_text: One is not a bearer of <s>Dharma</s> merely because one speaks much;

children.text: yo tu appam pi sottāna dhammaṃ kāyena phassaye |
children.translated_text: but one who, having heard even a little, touches the <s>Dharma</s> with the body,

children.text: sa ve dhammadharo hoti yo dhamme na pramajjati ||
children.translated_text: that one is truly a bearer of <s>Dharma</s>, who is not heedless regarding the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: na tāvatā dharmadharo yāvatā bahu bhāṣate |
children.translated_text: One is not a bearer of <s>Dharma</s> merely because one speaks much;

children.text: yas tv ihālpam api śrutvā dharmaṃ kāyena vai spṛśet |
children.translated_text: but one who, having heard even a little here, touches the <s>Dharma</s> with the body,

children.text: sa vai dharmadharo bhavati yo dharme na pramādyate ||
children.translated_text: that one is truly a bearer of <s>Dharma</s>, who is not heedless regarding the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: dhammaṃ vicinātha apramattā mā vo kāmaguṇā bhrameṃsu cittaṃ |
children.translated_text: Examine the <s>Dharma</s> heedfully! Let not the strands of sensual pleasure confuse your mind!

children.text: mā lohaguḍe gilaṃ pramatto kraṇḍe dukkham idan ti dahyamāno ||
children.translated_text: Do not, being heedless, swallow the iron ball — do not cry out "This is suffering!" while burning.

children.text: ātāpi vihara tvam apramatto mā te kāmaguṇo matheta cittam |
children.translated_text: Dwell ardently and heedfully! Let not the strands of sensual pleasure crush your mind!

children.text: mā lohaguḍāṃ gileḥ pramattaḥ krandaṃ vai narakeṣu pacyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not, being heedless, swallow the iron ball — do not cry out while being cooked in the hells!

body.translated_text: Chapter on Heedfulness (<s>Apramādavarga</s>)
***** The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> *****

children.text: chinna sūtraṃ parākrāmma bhavaṃ praṇuda brāhmaṇa |
children.translated_text: Cut the stream! Strive on, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! Drive away becoming!

children.text: saṃkhārāṇāṃ khayaṃ ñāttā akathaso si brāhmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: Having known the destruction of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), you are a knower of the uncreated, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: chindhi srotaḥ parākramya kāmāṃ praṇuda brāhmaṇa |
children.translated_text: Cut the stream! Strive on! Drive away sensual desires, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>!

children.text: saṃkārāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ jñātvā hy akṛtajño bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Having known the destruction of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), you shall become a knower of the uncreated.
From whomever one may learn the <s>Dharma</s>, whether old or young,

children.text: sakkacca naṃ namasseyā aggihotraṃ va brāhmaṇo ||
children.translated_text: one should respectfully honor him, as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> honors the sacrificial fire.

children.text: yasya dharmaṃ vijānīyād vṛddhasya daharasya vā |
children.translated_text: From whomever one may learn the <s>Dharma</s>, whether old or young,

children.text: satṛatyanaṃ namasyeta hy agnihotram iva dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should respectfully honor him, as a twice-born honors the sacrificial fire.
From whomever one may learn the <s>Dharma</s> taught by the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: tam eva apacāyeyā aggihotraṃ va brāhmaṇo ||
children.translated_text: one should honor that very person, as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> honors the sacrificial fire.
From whomever one may learn the <s>Dharma</s> taught by the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: satkṛtyainaṃ namasyeta hy agnihotram iva dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should respectfully honor him, as a twice-born honors the sacrificial fire.

children.text: na jaṭāhi na gotreṇa na jāccā hoti brāhmaṇo |
children.translated_text: Not by matted hair, not by clan, not by birth is one a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: yo tu bāhati pāpāni aṇutthūlāni sabbaśo ||
children.translated_text: but one who wards off evils, both small and great, in every way —

body.text: bāhanā eva pāpānāṃ brāhmaṇo ti pravuccati |

children.text: na jaṭābhir na gotreṇa na jātyā brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Not by matted hair, not by clan, not by birth is one considered a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: yas tu vāhayate pāpāny aṇusthūlāni sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: but he who drives away evils, small and great, in every way —

children.text: vāhitatvāt tu pāpānāṃ brāhmaṇo vai nirucyate ||
children.translated_text: because of having driven away evils, he is truly called a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: by warding off (<s>bāhana</s>) evils, one is called a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text:
38 Dhp401
vārī pukkharapatte vā ārāgre-r-iva sāsavo ||
body.translated_text:
38 Dhp401
As water on a lotus leaf, or a mustard seed on the tip of an awl —

body.text: yo na lippati kāmesu tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ |

children.translated_text: As water on a lotus leaf, or a mustard seed on the tip of an awl —

children.text: na lipyate yo hi kāmair bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi tam ||
children.translated_text: he who is not stained by sensual pleasures, him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: he who does not cling to sensual pleasures, him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text:
39 Dhp387
udayaṃ tapati ādicco rātrim ābhāti candramā ||
body.translated_text:
39 Dhp387
By day the sun shines, by night the moon glows;

body.text: sannaddho khattiyo tapati jhāyiṃ tapati brāhmaṇo ||
body.translated_text: armoured the <s>Kṣatriya</s> shines, in meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shines;

body.text: atha sabbe ahorātte buddho tapati tejasā ||
body.translated_text: but at all times, day and night, the <s>Buddha</s> shines with splendour.

children.text: divā tapati hādityo rātrāv ābhāti candramāḥ |
children.translated_text: By day the sun shines, by night the moon glows;

children.text: saṃnaddhaḥ kṣatriyas tapati dhyāyī tapati brāhmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: armoured the <s>Kṣatriya</s> shines, in meditation the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shines;

children.text: atha nityam ahorātraṃ buddhas tapati tejasā ||
children.translated_text: but always, day and night, the <s>Buddha</s> shines with splendour.

children.text: yassa pāram apāram vā pārāpāraṃ na vijjati |
children.translated_text: For whom there is neither the far shore, nor the near shore, nor both shores,

children.text: vītajjaraṃ visaṃyuttaṃ tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: free from distress, unfettered — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yadā dayesu dhammesu pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo |
children.translated_text: When in his own teachings (<s>dharma</s>) the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has gone beyond,

children.text: athassa sabbe saṃyogā atthaṃ gacchanti jānato ||
children.translated_text: then all his bonds come to an end, for he is one who knows.

children.text: yadā hi sveṣu dharmeṣu brāhmaṇaḥ pārago bhavet |
children.translated_text: When in his own teachings the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has gone beyond,
then all his bonds come to an end, for he is one who sees.
He indeed, whose bonds are destroyed, whose pride and rebirth are exhausted,

children.text: saṃghāvasevī dhammaṭṭho saṃghaṃ na upeti vedagū ||
children.translated_text: who dwells with the <s>Saṅgha</s>, established in <s>Dharma</s> — a knower of the <s>Vedas</s>, he does not approach the <s>Saṅgha</s> (for worldly reasons).

children.text: sa tu vikṣīṇa saṃyogaḥ kṣīṇamāno niraupadhiḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose bonds are destroyed, whose pride is exhausted, who is without attachment (<s>nirupadhi</s>) —

children.text: kāyasya bhedāt saprajñaḥ saṃkhyān nopaiti nirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the breaking up of the body, being wise, he does not enter into reckoning, being at peace (<s>nirvṛta</s>).
He who utters speech that is gentle, informative, and true,

children.text: tāya nābhiṣape kaṃci tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: by which he offends no one — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
He who always speaks words that are gentle and informative,

children.text: yayā nābhiṣajet kaś cid bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi tam ||
children.translated_text: by which he would offend no one — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Unentangled with householders and with homeless ones alike,

children.text: anokasāriṃ appicchaṃ tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: wandering without a home, of few wishes — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Unentangled with householders and with homeless ones alike,

children.text: anokasāriṇaṃ tuṣṭaṃ bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi taṃ ||
children.translated_text: wandering without a home, content — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yassa kāyena vācāya manasā nāsti dukkataṃ |
children.translated_text: He who has no wrongdoing by body, by speech, or by mind,

children.text: saṃvṛtaṃ trisu ṭṭhāesu tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: restrained in these three domains — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yasya kāyena vācā ca manasā ca na duṣkṛtam |
children.translated_text: He who has no wrongdoing by body, by speech, or by mind,

children.text: susaṃvṛtaṃ tṛbhiḥ sthānair bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi tam ||
children.translated_text: well-restrained in three domains — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: mā brāhmaṇassa prahare nāssa mucceya brāhmaṇo |
children.translated_text: One should not strike a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor should a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> give vent to anger against the striker;

children.text: dhi brāhmaṇassa hantāraṃ ya ssa vā su na muccati ||
children.translated_text: shame on the one who strikes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and greater shame on the one who gives vent to anger.

children.text: na brāhmaṇasya praharen na ca muñceta brāhmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not strike a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor should a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> release anger;

children.text: dhig brāhmaṇasya hantāraṃ dhik taṃ yaṣ ca pramuñcati ||
children.translated_text: shame on the one who strikes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and shame on the one who retaliates.

children.text: mātaraṃ paṭhanaṃ hantā rājānaṃ do ca khattiye |
children.translated_text: Having slain mother and father, and a king together with two learned <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,

children.text: rāṣṭaṃ sānucaraṃ hantā anigho carati brāhmaṇo ||
children.translated_text: having slain a kingdom with its followers, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> goes untroubled.

children.text: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ hatvā rājānaṃ dvau ca śrotriyau |
children.translated_text: Having slain mother and father, a king and two learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ sānucaraṃ hatvā anigho yāti brāhmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having slain a kingdom with its followers, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> goes untroubled.
Him of deep wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), intelligent, skilled in distinguishing the path from the non-path,

children.text: uttamāttham anuprāttaṃ tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: who has attained the highest goal — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Him of deep understanding, rich in intelligence, skilled in the path and the non-path,

children.text: uttamārtham anuprāptaṃ bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi tam ||
children.translated_text: who has attained the highest goal — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Meditating, free from passion, seated, whose task is done, free from <s>āsravas</s> (mental defilements),

children.text: uttamāttham anuprāttaṃ tam ahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: who has attained the highest goal — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
The meditator, free from passion, whose task is done, free from <s>āsravas</s>,

children.text: kṣīṇāsravaṃ visaṃyuktaṃ bravīmi brāhmaṇaṃ hi tam ||
children.translated_text: whose defilements are exhausted, who is unfettered — him I call a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: Chapter on the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>
***** <s>Bhikṣu</s> (Monk) *****

children.text: sabbattha saṃvaro sādhu sādhu sabbattha saṃvaro |
children.translated_text: Restraint in all things is good; good is restraint in all things;
the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) restrained in all things is freed from all suffering.

children.text: kāyena samvaro sādhu sādhu vācāya saṃvaro |
children.translated_text: Restraint of body is good, good is restraint of speech;

children.text: manasā pi saṃvaro sādhu sādhu sabbattha saṃvaro |
children.translated_text: restraint of mind is good, good is restraint in all things;
the <s>bhikṣu</s> restrained in all things is freed from all suffering.

children.text: kāyena saṃvaraḥ sādhu sādhu vācā ca saṃvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Restraint of body is good, good is restraint of speech;

children.text: manasā saṃvaraḥ sādhu sādhu sarvatra saṃvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: restraint of mind is good, good is restraint in all things;
the <s>bhikṣu</s> restrained in all things is freed from all suffering.

body.translated_text:
52 Dhp362
With hands restrained, with feet restrained, with speech restrained, with senses well-controlled,

body.text: ajjhattarato samāhito eko saṃtuṣito tam āhu bhikkhuṃ |

children.translated_text: With hands restrained, with feet restrained, with speech restrained, fully restrained in all,

children.text: ādhyātmarataḥ samāhito hy ekaḥ saṃtuṣito hi yaḥ sa bhikṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: delighting inwardly, composed, solitary, content — he is a <s>bhikṣu</s>.

body.translated_text: delighting inwardly, composed, solitary, content — him they call a <s>bhikṣu</s>.

53 Dhp378
With body calmed, with mind calmed, with speech calmed, well-composed,

children.translated_text: With body calmed, (with mind calmed,) with speech calmed, well-composed,
the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has rejected the world's bait is declared 'one at peace.'

body.translated_text: the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has rejected the world's bait is called 'one at peace.'

body.text:
54 Dhp363
yo mukhe saṃyyato bhikkhū mantābhāṣī anuddhato ||
body.translated_text:
54 Dhp363
The <s>bhikṣu</s> who is restrained in speech, who speaks wisely, who is not agitated —

body.text: atthaṃ dhammañ ca deśeti madhuraṃ tassa bhāṣitaṃ |

children.text: mukhena saṃyato bhikṣur mandābhāṣī hy anuddhataḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣu</s> restrained in speech, speaking deliberately, not agitated —

children.text: arthaṃ dharmaṃ ca deśayati madhuraṃ tasya bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: who teaches the meaning and the <s>Dharma</s>, sweet is his speech.

body.translated_text: who teaches the meaning and the <s>Dharma</s>, sweet is his speech.

body.text:
55 Dhp365
saṃ lābhaṃ nātimaṃñeyā nā 'ṃñesaṃ prihayaṃ care ||
body.translated_text:
55 Dhp365
One should not despise one's own gains, nor should one go about envying others;

children.translated_text: One should not despise one's own gains, nor should one be covetous of others';
the <s>bhikṣu</s> who covets others' gains does not attain <s>samādhi</s>.

body.translated_text: the <s>bhikṣu</s> who envies others does not attain <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text:
56 Dhp366
appalābho pi ce bhikkhū saṃ lābhaṃ nātimaṃñati ||
body.translated_text:
56 Dhp366
Even if a <s>bhikṣu</s> receives little, if he does not despise his own gains,

body.text: taṃ ve devā praśaṃsanti śuddhājīviṃ atandritaṃ ||
body.translated_text: the gods praise him — one of pure livelihood, diligent.

children.translated_text: Even if one is of little renown, if one is well-composed in moral conduct,
the wise praise him — one of pure livelihood, diligent.

children.text: siñca bhikkhu imaṃ nāvāṃ sittā te laghu hehiti |
children.translated_text: Bail out this boat, O <s>bhikṣu</s>! When bailed, it will go lightly for you;

children.text: hettā rāgañ ca doṣaṃ ca tato nibbāṇam ehisi ||
children.translated_text: having cut away lust and hatred, from there you will reach <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: siñca bhikṣor imāṃ nāvaṃ siktā laghvī bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Bail out this boat, O <s>bhikṣu</s>! When bailed, it will become light;

children.text: hitvā rāgaṃ ca doṣaṃ ca tato nirvāṇam eṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned lust and hatred, from there you will reach <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.translated_text:
58
With uplifted mind, joyful, having overcome the pleasant and the unpleasant —

children.translated_text: then, full of gladness, mindful, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth.
With uplifted mind, joyful, having overcome the pleasant and the unpleasant —

body.translated_text: full of gladness, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should attain the destruction of suffering.

59 Dhp368
The <s>bhikṣu</s> who dwells in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), who has faith in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.translated_text: would attain the peaceful state, the stilling of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), which is bliss,

children.text: dṛṣṭe va dhamme nibbāṇaṃ yogacchemaṃ anuttaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: <s>nirvāṇa</s> in this very life, the supreme security from bondage.
The <s>bhikṣu</s> who dwells in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), who has faith in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>,
would attain the peaceful state, the stilling of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), which is bliss.

body.translated_text: (<s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this very life, the supreme security from bondage.)

children.translated_text: For the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has entered an empty dwelling, whose mind is calmed,

children.text: amānuṣā ratī hoti sammaṃ dhammaṃ vipaśśato ||
children.translated_text: there arises a superhuman delight, as he rightly contemplates the <s>Dharma</s>.
For the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has entered an empty dwelling, who is self-exerted,

children.text: amānuṣā ratir bhavati samyag dharmāṃ vipaśyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: there arises a superhuman delight, as he rightly contemplates the <s>Dharma</s>.
Whenever one thoroughly comprehends the arising and passing away of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),

children.text: labhate cittassa prāmojjaṃ amatā hetaṃ vijānato ||
children.translated_text: one obtains joy of mind — for one who knows, this is the deathless.
Whenever one thoroughly touches the arising and passing away of the <s>skandhas</s>,

children.text: prāmodyaṃ labhate tatra prīyā sukham analpakam |
children.translated_text: one obtains gladness there, joy, and no small happiness;
then, full of gladness, mindful, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth.

children.text: nāsti jhānam apraṃñassa praṃñā nāsti ajhāyato |
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) without <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and no <s>prajñā</s> without <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: yamhi jhānaṃ ca praṃñā ca sa ve nibbāṇasantike ||
children.translated_text: in whom there is both <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>, he is truly near <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: nāsty aprajñasya vai dhyānam prajñā nādhyāyato 'sti ca |
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dhyāna</s> for one without <s>prajñā</s>, and no <s>prajñā</s> for one without <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: yasya dhyānaṃ tathā prajñā sa vai nirvāṇasāntike ||
children.translated_text: in whom there is both <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>, he is truly near <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: tatthāyam ādī bhavati iha praṃñassa bhikkhuṇo |
children.translated_text: This is the beginning for the wise <s>bhikṣu</s> here:
guarding of the senses, contentment, and restraint in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code).
Uv32:26cd,27ab

children.text: tasyāyam ādir bhavati tathā prajñasya bhikṣuṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is the beginning for the wise <s>bhikṣu</s>:

children.text: saṃtuṣṭir indriyair guptiḥ prātimokṣe ca saṃvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: contentment, guarding of the senses, and restraint in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>.
One should associate with good friends, of pure livelihood, diligent;
one should be hospitable in conduct, skilled in proper behaviour;
then, full of gladness, mindful, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth.

children.text: mātraṃ bhajeta pratirūpaṃ śuddhājīvo bhavet sadā |
children.translated_text: One should associate with suitable friends, one should always be of pure livelihood;
one should be hospitable in conduct, skilled in proper behaviour;
then, full of gladness, mindful, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth.

children.text: atthesu jātesu sukhā sakhāyā puṃñaṃ sukhaṃ jīvitasaṃkhayamhi |
children.translated_text: When need arises, friends are a blessing; merit is a blessing at the end of life;

children.text: toṣṭī sukhā yā itarī[ ] sabbassa pāpassa sukhaṃ prahāṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: contentment with whatever comes is a blessing; the abandoning of all evil is a blessing.

children.text: artheṣu jāteṣu sukhaṃ sahāyāḥ puṇyaṃ sukhaṃ jīvitasaṃkṣayeṣu |
children.translated_text: When need arises, companions are a blessing; merit is a blessing at the end of life;

children.text: tuṣṭiḥ sukhā yā tv itaretareṇa sarvasya duḥkhasya sukho nirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: contentment with whatever comes is a blessing; the cessation of all suffering is a blessing.

children.text: sukhā mātretā loke tato pettetā sukhā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is motherhood in the world, and blessed too is fatherhood;

children.text: śāmannatā sukhā loke tato brāhmannatā sukhā ||
children.translated_text: blessed is the state of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) in the world, and blessed too is the state of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sukhaṃ mātṛvyatā loke sukhaṃ caiva pittṛvyatā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is the state of a mother in the world, and blessed too is the state of a father;

children.text: sukhaṃ śrāmaṇyatā loke tathā brāhmaṇyatā sukham ||
children.translated_text: blessed is the state of a <s>śramaṇa</s> in the world, and likewise blessed is the state of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sukhaṃ yāvaj jarā śīlaṃ sukhā śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) that endures until old age; blessed is faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) well established;

children.text: sukhā attharasā vācā assiṃ mānakkhayo sukho ||
children.translated_text: blessed is speech filled with meaning; blessed is the destruction of pride.

children.text: sukhaṃ yāvaj jarā śīlaṃ sukhaṃ śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) that endures until old age; blessed is faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) well established;
blessed is speech delighting in meaning; blessed is the non-doing of evil.

children.text: sukho buddhāna uppādo sukhā dhammassa deśanā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>; blessed is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: sukhā saṃghassa sāmaggrī samaggrāṇāṃ tapo sukho ||
children.translated_text: blessed is the harmony of the <s>Saṅgha</s>; blessed is the austerity of those in harmony.

children.text: sukhaṃ buddhasya cotpādaḥ sukhaṃ dharmasya deśanā |
children.translated_text: Blessed is the arising of the <s>Buddha</s>; blessed is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: sukhaṃ saṃghasya sāmagrī samagrāṇāṃ tapaḥ sukhaṃ ||
children.translated_text: blessed is the harmony of the <s>Saṅgha</s>; blessed is the austerity of those in harmony.

children.text: sukhaṃ daṃśanam ayirāṇāṃ saṃvāso pi satāṃ sukho |
children.translated_text: Blessed is the sight of the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>); blessed too is their company always;

children.text: addaṃśanena bālānāṃ niccam eva sukhī siyā ||
children.translated_text: by not seeing fools, one would always be happy.

children.text: sukhaṃ darśanam āryāṇāṃ saṃvāso 'pi sadā sukhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Blessed is the sight of the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>); blessed too is their company always;

children.text: adarśanena bālānāṃ nityam eva sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: by not seeing fools, one would always be happy.
For one who travels in the company of fools grieves for a long time;
painful is the company of fools, as with enemies, always;

children.text: dhīrā tu sukhasaṃvāsā ñātīnaṃ vā samāgamo ||
children.translated_text: but the company of the wise is pleasant, like a gathering of kinsmen.
For one who travels in the company of fools grieves along the long road;

children.text: duḥkho bālair hi saṃvāso hy amitrair iva sarvaśāḥ |
children.translated_text: painful is the company of fools, as with enemies, always;

children.text: dhīrais tu sukhasaṃvāso jñātīnām ivā saṃgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the company of the wise is pleasant, like a gathering of kinsmen.

children.text: tassā hi dhīraṃ ca bahuśśutañ ca dhoreyaśīlavratamantam ayiraṃ |
children.translated_text: Therefore one should follow the wise, the learned, the steadfast, the virtuous and dutiful, the noble one;

children.text: taṃ tārisaṃ sappuruṣaṃ sumedhaṃ sevetha nakkhattapathe va candramā ||
children.translated_text: such a good person, of great wisdom, one should follow as the moon follows the path of the stars.
One should attend upon the wise, the learned, the virtuous, the greatly learned,
the steadfast, endowed with energy — as the stars attend upon the moon.

children.text: priyāto jāyate dukkhaṃ priyā śokā priyā bhayaṃ |
children.translated_text: From what is dear arises sorrow, from what is dear arises fear;

children.text: priyāto vipramuttassa nāsti śokā kato bhayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: for one wholly freed from what is dear, there is no sorrow — whence fear?
Uv5:1

children.text: priyebhyo jāyate śokaḥ priyebhyo jāyate bhayam |
children.translated_text: From those who are dear arises sorrow, from those who are dear arises fear;

children.text: priyebhyo vipramuktānāṃ nāsti śokaḥ kuto bhayam ||
children.translated_text: for those freed from what is dear, there is no sorrow — whence fear?
Do not meet with those who are dear, nor ever with those who are not dear;

children.text: priyassa addaṃśanaṃ dukkhaṃ apriyassa ca daṃśanaṃ ||
children.translated_text: not seeing what is dear is painful, and so too is the sight of what is not dear.
Uv5:5

children.text: mā priyaiḥ saṃgamo jātu mā ca syād apriyaiḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Let there never be union with the dear, nor ever with the unpleasant;

children.text: priyāṇām adarśanaṃ duḥkhaṃ apriyāṇāṃ ca darśanam ||
children.translated_text: Not seeing the dear is suffering, and seeing the unpleasant [is suffering too].

children.text: tassā priyaṃ na kayirātha priyāvādo hi pāpako |
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not make anything dear, for attachment to the dear is evil;

children.text: ggraṃthā tesaṃ na vijjanti yesaṃ nāsti priyāpriyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: There are no bonds for those for whom there is no dear or unpleasant.
Uv5:8

children.text: tasmāt priyaṃ na karvīta priyabhāvo hi pāpakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not make anything dear, for the state of attachment is evil;

children.text: granthās teṣāṃ na vidyante yeṣāṃ nāsti priyāpriyam ||
children.translated_text: There are no bonds for those for whom there is no dear or unpleasant.
Hunger is the foremost of diseases, conditioned things are the foremost suffering;
Knowing this as it truly is, <s>Nibbāna</s> (extinction) is the foremost happiness.

children.text: kṣudhā parama rogāṇāṃ saṃskārā duḥkham eva tu |
children.translated_text: Hunger is the foremost of diseases, <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) are indeed suffering;
Knowing this as it truly is, one should [aspire to] the supreme <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
Health is the foremost gain, contentment is the foremost wealth;
Trust is the foremost kinsman, <s>Nibbāna</s> is the foremost happiness.
Health is the foremost gain, contentment is the foremost wealth;
A trustworthy friend is the foremost [companion], <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is the foremost happiness.
If by abandoning small pleasures one would see abundant happiness,

children.text: caje māttāsukhaṃ dhīro saṃpaśśaṃ vipulaṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: the wise one should abandon small pleasures, seeing abundant happiness.
If by relinquishing small pleasures one would see abundant happiness,

children.text: tyajen mātrāsukhaṃ dhīraḥ saṃpaśyaṃ vipulaṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: the wise one should relinquish small pleasures, seeing abundant happiness.

children.text: manujassa sadā satīmato māttaṃ jāniya laddhibhojane |
children.translated_text: For a person who is always mindful, knowing the right measure in food obtained,

children.text: tanukā 'ssa bhavanti vedanā śanikaṃ jīrati āyu pālayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: his feelings become diminished; he ages slowly, preserving his lifespan.
For a person who is always mindful, who knows the right measure in food obtained,

children.text: tanukāsya bhavanti vedanāḥ śanakair jīryati āyuḥ pālayam ||
children.translated_text: his feelings become diminished; he ages slowly, preserving his lifespan.

children.text: dullabho puruṣājaṃño na so sabbattha jāyati |
children.translated_text: Rare is a noble person; he is not born everywhere;

children.text: yattha so jāyate vīro taṃ kulaṃ sukham edhati ||
children.translated_text: wherever that hero is born, that family prospers in happiness.

children.text: durlabhaḥ puruṣo jātyo nāsau sarvatra jāyati |
children.translated_text: Rare is a well-born person; he is not born everywhere;

children.text: yatrāsau jāyate vīras tat kulaṃ sukham edhate ||
children.translated_text: wherever that hero is born, that family prospers in happiness.
80 Dhp83

children.text: sabbattha ve sappuruṣā bhavanti na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo |
children.translated_text: Everywhere the good are modest; the virtuous do not chatter for the sake of pleasures;

children.text: sukhena puṭṭhā uttavā dukhena noccāvacaṃ sappuruṣā karonti ||
children.translated_text: whether touched by happiness or by suffering, the good do not show elation or depression.

children.text: sāpatrapāḥ satpuruṣā bhavanti na kāmahetor lapayanti santaḥ |
children.translated_text: The good are modest; the virtuous do not chatter for the sake of pleasures;

children.text: spṛṣṭā hi dukhena tathā sukhena noccāvacāḥ satpuruṣā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: whether touched by suffering or by happiness, the good do not become elated or depressed.

children.text: jayaṃ veraṃ prasavati dukhaṃ śeti parājito |
children.translated_text: Victory breeds enmity; the defeated one sleeps in suffering;
the peaceful one sleeps happily, having abandoned both victory and defeat.

children.text: jayād vairaṃ prasavate duḥkhaṃ śete parājitaḥ |
children.translated_text: From victory enmity is born; the defeated one sleeps in suffering;
the peaceful one sleeps happily, having abandoned both victory and defeat.
82 Dhp333cd

children.text: sukhā najjo sūpatitthā sukho dhammajito jano |
children.translated_text: Happy is a river with good fords; happy is a people conquered by <s>Dharma</s>;
happy is the gain of faith; happy is the non-doing of evil.

children.text: sukhā nadī sūpatīrthā sukhaṃ dharmajino jinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Happy is a river with good fords; happy is the <s>Dharma</s>-victor, the conqueror;
the gain of wisdom is always happy; happy is the non-doing of evil.

children.text: sukhaṃ draṣṭuṃ śīlavanto sukhaṃ draṣṭuṃ bahuśśutā |
children.translated_text: Happy it is to see the virtuous; happy it is to see the learned;

children.text: arahanto pi sukhaṃ draṣṭuṃ vipramuttā niropadhī ||
children.translated_text: happy it is to see the <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones), freed and without acquisitions.

children.text: śīlavantaḥ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭuṃ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭuṃ bahuśrutāḥ |
children.translated_text: Happy it is to see the virtuous; happy it is to see the learned;
and happy it is to see the <s>Arhats</s>, freed from rebirth.

children.text: ye keci śokā paridevitaṃ vā dukkhaṃ va lokamhi anekarūpaṃ |
children.translated_text: Whatever sorrows, lamentations, or sufferings of manifold kinds exist in the world,

children.text: priyaṃ paṭicca prabhavati ete priye asante na bhavanti ete ||
children.translated_text: these arise dependent on the dear; when the dear does not exist, these do not arise.
Uv5:3

children.text: śokā hi vai paridevitaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca lokasya hi naikarūpam |
children.translated_text: Sorrows indeed, and lamentations, and suffering of manifold kinds in the world,

children.text: priyaṃ pratītyeha tad asti sarvaṃ priye 'sati syān na kathaṃ cid etat ||
children.translated_text: all this exists dependent on the dear; when the dear does not exist, none of this would be.

children.text: tassā hi te sukhi<khi>no vītaśokā yesaṃ priyaṃ nāsti like |
children.translated_text: Therefore those are happy and free from sorrow for whom there is no dear one in the world;

children.text: tassā aśokaṃ virajaṃ prātthayānā priyaṃ na kayirātha kahiṃci loke ||
children.translated_text: therefore, aspiring to the sorrowless and stainless state, one should not make anything dear in the world.
Uv5:4

children.text: tasmād dhi te sukhitā vītaśokā yeṣāṃ priyaṃ nāsti kathaṃ cid eva |
children.translated_text: Therefore those are happy and free from sorrow for whom there is nothing dear at all;

children.text: tasmād aśokaṃ padam eṣamāṇaḥ priyaṃ na kurvīta hi jīvaloke ||
children.translated_text: therefore, seeking the sorrowless state, one should not make anything dear in the world of the living.
86 Dhp90
For one who has completed the journey, who is free from sorrow, who is liberated in every way,
who has abandoned all bonds — there is no burning.
For one who has completed the journey, who is free from sorrow, who is liberated, the protector,
who has abandoned all bonds — there is no burning.
87 Dhp90
For those who have no accumulation, who have fully understood [the nature of] food,

children.text: ākāśe va śakuntānāṃ padaṃ tesāṃ durannayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: their path is hard to trace, like that of birds in the sky.
Uv29:25abef
For those who have no accumulation, who have fully understood [the nature of] food,
their path is hard to follow, like that of birds in the sky.
88 Dhp96

children.text: śānto tassa mano hoti śāntā vācā ca kaṃmu ca |
children.translated_text: Peaceful is his mind, peaceful are his speech and action,
for one who is liberated through right knowledge, who is at peace, the protector.

children.text: śāntam asya mano bhavati śāntā vāk kāyakarma ca |
children.translated_text: Peaceful is his mind, peaceful are his speech and bodily action,
for one who is liberated through right knowledge, the monk who is at peace.
89 Dhp94

children.text: yassendriyāṇi samataṃ gatāni aśśā yathā sārathinā sudāntā |
children.translated_text: He whose senses have reached equanimity, like horses well-tamed by a charioteer,

children.text: prahīṇamānassa anāsavassa devā pi tassa prihayanti tāyino ||
children.translated_text: who has abandoned pride and is free from taints — even the gods envy such a protector.

children.text: yasyendriyāṇi samatāṃ gatāni aśvo yathā sārathinā sudāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose senses have reached equanimity, like a horse well-tamed by a charioteer,

children.text: prahīṇadoṣāya nirāsravāya devāpi tasmai spṛhayanti nityam ||
children.translated_text: who has abandoned faults and is free from taints — even the gods always envy him.
The tamed one is led into the assembly; the tamed one the king mounts;
the tamed one is the best among humans — he who endures harsh speech.

children.text: dānto vai samitiṃ yāti dāntaṃ rājādhirohati |
children.translated_text: The tamed one indeed goes to the assembly; the tamed one the king mounts;
the tamed one is the best among humans — he who endures harsh words.

children.text: varam assatarā dāntā ājāneyā va sendhavā |
children.translated_text: Excellent are tamed mules, and thoroughbred horses of <s>Sindh</s>,

children.text: kuñjarā va mahānāgā āttā dānto tato varaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and great elephants; but one who has tamed himself is better than them.

children.text: yo hy aśvaṃ damayej jānyam ājāneyaṃ ca saindhavam |
children.translated_text: He who would tame a noble horse, a thoroughbred of <s>Sindh</s>,

children.text: kuñjaraṃ vā mahānāgam ātmā dāntas tato varam ||
children.translated_text: or a great elephant — one who has tamed himself is better than that.

children.text: na hi tehi jānajātehi tāṃ bhūmim abhisaṃbhave |
children.translated_text: For not by those vehicles could one reach the untrodden land,
as one who is well-tamed, by the tamed [self], goes [there] by means of the tamed.

children.text: na hi tena sa yānena tāṃ bhūmim abhisaṃbhavet |
children.translated_text: For not by that vehicle could one reach that land

children.text: yām ātmanā sudāntena dānto dāntena gacchati ||
children.translated_text: to which one who is well-tamed, by the tamed [self], goes by means of the tamed.
93 Dhp81

children.text: śelo yathā ekaghano vātena na samīrati |
children.translated_text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the wind,
so the wise are not shaken by blame and praise.

children.text: śailo yathāpy ekaghano vāyunā na prakampyate |
children.translated_text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the wind,
so the wise are not shaken by blame and praise.
94 Dhp9
He who, not free from impurity, would wear the yellow robe,

children.text: apeto damasaccena na so kāṣāyam arihati ||
children.translated_text: devoid of self-control and truth — he is not worthy of the yellow robe.
He who, not free from impurity, would wear the yellow robe,
devoid of self-control and gentleness — he is not worthy of the yellow robe.
95 Dhp10
But he who has cast off impurity, who is well-composed in virtues,

children.text: upeto damasaccena sa ve kāṣāyam arihati ||
children.translated_text: endowed with self-control and truth — he is indeed worthy of the yellow robe.

children.text: yas tu vāntakaṣāyaḥ syāc chīleṣu susamāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: But he who has cast off impurity, who is well-composed in virtues,
endowed with self-control and gentleness — he is indeed worthy of the yellow robe.

body.translated_text: Sorrow chapter (<s>Śokavarga</s>)
***** Kalyāṇī (Auspicious Deeds) *****

children.translated_text: One should hasten toward the good and restrain the mind from evil;

children.text: dhaṃdhaṃ hi karato puṃñaṃ pāpamhi ramate mano ||
children.translated_text: for when one performs merit sluggishly, the mind delights in evil.
One should hasten toward the good and restrain the mind from evil;

children.text: dhandhaṃ hi kurvataḥ puṇyaṃ pāpeṣu ramate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for when one performs merit sluggishly, the mind delights in evil.

children.text: kayira ce puruṣo pāpaṃ na naṃ kayirā punappuno |
children.translated_text: If a person has done evil, he should not do it again and again;

children.text: na tamhi chanda[ṃ] kayirātha dukkho pāpassa sa[ṃ]cayo ||
children.translated_text: he should not find pleasure in it, for the accumulation of evil is painful.

children.text: karyāc cet puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ nainaṃ kuryāt punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: If a person has done evil, he should not do it again and again;

children.text: na tatra cchandaṃ kurvīta duḥkhaṃ pāpasya saṃcayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should not develop a liking for it, for the accumulation of evil is painful.

children.text: kayira ce puruṣo pu[ṃ]ña[ṃ] kay[i]ra cena[ṃ] punappuno |
children.translated_text: If a person has done merit, he should do it again and again;

children.text: tamh[i] eva chanda[ṃ] kayirātha sukho puṃñassa saṃcayo ||
children.translated_text: he should find pleasure in it, for the accumulation of merit is happiness.

children.text: kuryāt tu puruṣaḥ puṇyaṃ kuryāc cainaṃ punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: A person should perform merit, and should do it again and again;

children.text: tatra cchandaṃ ca kurvīta sukhaṃ puṇyasya saṃcayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should develop a liking for it, for the accumulation of merit is happiness.
For the pure one, every day is the <s>phālguna</s> festival; for the pure one, every day is the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day);
for the pure one of clean deeds, the vow is always fulfilled.

children.text: śuddhasya hi sadā phalguḥ śuddasya poṣathaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: For the pure one, every day is the <s>phālguna</s>; for the pure one, every day is the <s>poṣatha</s>;
for the pure one of clean deeds, the vow is always fulfilled.
100 Dhp314ab

children.text: akataṃ dukkataṃ śreyo pacchā tapati dukkataṃ |
children.translated_text: Better is the undone than the ill-done; the ill-done burns afterward;

children.text: dukkataṃ me kataṃ ti śocati bhūyo śocati doggatiṃ gato ||
children.translated_text: having done an ill deed, he grieves, saying 'An ill deed was done by me'; he grieves even more gone to a bad destination.

children.text: akṛtaṃ kukṛtāc chreyaḥ paścāt tapati duṣkṛtaṃ |
children.translated_text: Better is the undone than the ill-done; the ill-done burns afterward;

children.text: śocate duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtvā śocate durgatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having done an ill deed, one grieves; one grieves [again] gone to a bad destination.
101 Dhp314cd

children.text: katañ ca sukataṃ sādhu yaṃ kattā nānutappati |
children.translated_text: And a well-done deed is good, that which the doer does not regret;

children.text: sukataṃ me kataṃ ti nandati bhūyo nandati soggatiṅ gato ||
children.translated_text: having done a good deed, he rejoices, saying 'A good deed was done by me'; he rejoices even more gone to a good destination.

children.text: kṛtaṃ tu sukṛtaṃ śreyo yat kṛtvā nānutapyate |
children.translated_text: A well-done deed is better, that which one does not regret after doing;

children.text: nandate sukṛtaṃ kṛtvā nandate sogatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having done a good deed, one rejoices; one rejoices gone to a good destination.

children.text: pāpo pi paśśate bhadraṃ yāva pāpaṃ na paccati |
children.translated_text: Even an evildoer sees good as long as evil has not ripened;

children.text: yadā tu paccate pāpaṃ atha pāpo pāpāni paśśati ||
children.translated_text: but when evil ripens, then the evildoer sees [only] evil.

children.text: pāpo 'pi paśyate bhadraṃ yāvat pāpaṃ na pacyate |
children.translated_text: Even an evildoer sees good as long as evil has not ripened;

children.text: yadā tu pacyate pāpam atha pāpāni paśyati ||
children.translated_text: but when evil ripens, then he sees [only] evil.

children.text: bhadro pi paśśate pāpaṃ yāva bhadraṃ na paccati |
children.translated_text: Even a good person sees evil as long as good has not ripened;

children.text: yadā tu paccate bhadraṃ atha bhadro bhadrāṇi paśśati ||
children.translated_text: but when good ripens, then the good person sees [only] good.

children.text: bhadro 'pi paśyate pāpaṃ yāvad bhadraṃ na pacyate |
children.translated_text: Even a good person sees evil as long as good has not ripened;

children.text: yadā tu pacyate bhadram atha bhadrāṇi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: but when good ripens, then he sees [only] good.

children.text: pāpaṃ pi karato bhadraṃ yāva pāpaṃ na paccati |
children.translated_text: Even while doing evil, [one sees] good as long as evil has not ripened;

children.text: atha payirāgate kāle pāpo pāpāni paśśati ||
children.translated_text: but when the time arrives, the evildoer sees [only] evil.

children.text: bhadraṃ pi karato pāpaṃ yāva bhadraṃ na paccati |
children.translated_text: Even while doing good, [one sees] evil as long as good has not ripened;

children.text: atha payirāgate kāle bhadro bhadrāṇi paśśati ||
children.translated_text: but when the time arrives, the good person sees [only] good.

children.text: pāṇimhi ce vraṇo nā 'ssa dhāreyā pāṇinā viṣaṃ |
children.translated_text: If there were no wound in the hand, one could carry poison in the hand;

children.text: nāvraṇe viṣam anneti nāsti pāpam akurvvato ||
children.translated_text: poison does not penetrate one without a wound — there is no evil for one who does not do [evil].

children.text: pāṇau cāsya vraṇo na syād dhārayet pāṇinā viṣam |
children.translated_text: If there were no wound in his hand, he could carry poison in the hand;

children.text: nāvraṇe krāmati viṣam nāsti pāpam akurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: poison does not pass into one without a wound — there is no evil for one who does not do [evil].

children.text: na hi pāpakaṃ kataṃ kammaṃ sajjaṃ chīram va mucchati |
children.translated_text: An evil deed done does not immediately curdle, like milk;

children.text: dahantaṃ bālam anneti bhassachanno va pāpako ||
children.translated_text: smoldering, it follows the fool, like fire covered with ashes.

children.text: na hi pāpakṛtaṃ karma sadyaḥ kṣīram iva mūrchati |
children.translated_text: An evil deed done does not immediately curdle, like milk;
burning, it follows the fool, like fire covered with ashes.

children.text: na hi pāpakaṃ kataṃ kammaṃ sajjaṃ śastam va kantati |
children.translated_text: An evil deed done does not immediately cut, like a weapon;

children.text: maraṇo 'peto hi jānāti yā gatī pāpakaṃmuno ||
children.translated_text: at the time of death one knows what is the destination of an evildoer.

children.text: na hi pāpakṛtaṃ karma sadyaṃ śastram iva kṛntati |
children.translated_text: An evil deed done does not immediately cut, like a weapon;

children.text: sāmparāye tu jānāti yā gatiḥ pāpakarmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: but in the hereafter one knows what is the destination of evildoers.

children.text: anāgataṃ paṭikayirātha kiccaṃ mā vo kiccaṃ kiccakāle vyadheyā |
children.translated_text: One should attend to one's duty before [it is due]; let not duty oppress you at the time of duty;

children.text: taṃ tārisaṃ paṭikatakiccakāriṃ na naṃ kiccaṃ kiccakāle vyadhehi ||
children.translated_text: for one who acts with duty attended to in time — duty does not oppress him at the time of duty.

children.text: pūrvaṃ hi kṛtyaṃ pratijāgareta mā me kṛtyaṃ kṛtyakāle vihanyāt |
children.translated_text: One should be vigilant about duty beforehand; let not duty obstruct me at the time of duty;

children.text: taṃ nityakāle pratiyatyakāriṇaṃ naiva kṛtyaṃ kṛtyakāle vihanti ||
children.translated_text: for one who always acts with duty attended to in time — duty does not obstruct him at the time of duty.

children.text: paṭikacceva taṃ kayirā yaṃ ñāyyā hitam āttano |
children.translated_text: One should do beforehand what one knows to be beneficial to oneself;

children.text: na śākaṭikamanti ssa mantaṃ dhīro parākrame ||
children.translated_text: the wise one should not proceed sluggishly, [pondering] with the thoughts of a cart-driver.

children.text: pratiyatyeva tat kuryād yaj jānrd dhitam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should do beforehand what one knows to be beneficial to oneself;
the wise one should not proceed sluggishly with the worries of a cart-driver.

children.text: yathā śākaṭiko māggaṃ samaṃ hettā mahāpathaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as a cart-driver, leaving the smooth highway,

children.text: viṣamaṃ māggam āsājja akkhachinno tha jhāyati ||
children.translated_text: and taking a rough path, grieves with a broken axle —

children.text: yathā śākaṭiko mārgaṃ samaṃ hitvā mahāpatham |
children.translated_text: Just as a cart-driver, leaving the smooth highway,

children.text: viṣamaṃ mārgam āgamya cchinnākṣaḥ śocate bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and taking a rough path, grieves greatly with a broken axle —
Thus having departed from <s>dharma</s> and having followed <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: bālo maccumukhaṃ prātto akkhachinno va jhāyati ||
children.translated_text: the fool, having reached the mouth of death, broods like one whose axle is broken.

children.text: evaṃ dharmād apakramya hy adharmam anuvartya ca |
children.translated_text: Thus having departed from <s>dharma</s> and having followed <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: bālo mṛtyuvaśaṃ prātac chinnākṣa iva śocate ||
children.translated_text: the fool, having fallen under death's power, grieves like one whose axle is broken.
Many who wear the saffron robe around their necks are of evil nature and unrestrained;

children.text: pāpā pāpehi kaṃmehi nirayaṃ te upapajjatha ||
children.translated_text: by their evil deeds, these evil ones are reborn in hell.
Many who wear the saffron robe around their necks are of evil nature and unrestrained;

children.text: pāpā hi karmabhiḥ pāpair ito gacchanti durgatim ||
children.translated_text: by their evil deeds, these evil ones go from here to a bad destination.

children.text: abhūtavādī nirayaṃ upeti yo cāpi kattā na karomī ti āha |
children.translated_text: The speaker of falsehood goes to hell, as does he who, having done [a deed], says 'I did not do it';

children.text: ubho pi te precca samā bhavanti nihīnakaṃmā manujā paratra ||
children.translated_text: both of them, after death, become equal — humans of base deeds in the next world.
Uv8:1

children.text: abhūtavādī narakān upaiti yaś cānyad apy ācaratīha karma |
children.translated_text: The speaker of falsehood goes to the hells, as does he who, having done one deed here, [claims] otherwise;

children.text: ubhau hi tau pretya samau niruktau nihīnadharmau manujau paratra ||
children.translated_text: both of them, after death, are declared equal — humans of base nature in the next world.

children.text: yo apraduṣṭassa naro praduṣyati śuddhassa poṣassa anaṃganassa |
children.translated_text: The man who wrongs one who is without fault, who is pure, a householder, without blemish —

children.text: tam eva bālaṃ pracceti pāpaṃ sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṃ va khito ||
children.translated_text: the evil returns upon that very fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.

children.text: yo hy apraduṣṭasya narasya duṣyate śuddhasya nityaṃ vigatāṅgaṇasya |
children.translated_text: He who wrongs a man who is without fault, who is ever pure and without blemish —

children.text: tam eva bālaṃ pratyāti pāpaṃ kṣiptaṃ rajaḥ prativātaṃ yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: the evil returns upon that very fool, just as dust thrown against the wind.

children.text: vāṇijo va bhayaṃ va māggaṃ appasāttho mahaddhano |
children.translated_text: Just as a merchant with few companions and great wealth [avoids] a dangerous road,
and as one who desires to live [avoids] poison, so should one avoid evil deeds.

children.text: vaṇig vā sabhayaṃ mārgaṃ alpaśāstro mahādhano |
children.translated_text: Just as a merchant with few guards and great wealth [avoids] a dangerous road,
and as one who desires to live [avoids] poison, so should one avoid evil deeds.
He who wishes for his own happiness through the infliction of suffering on others,
entangled in the web of hatred, is not freed from suffering.
He who would wish for his own happiness through the infliction of suffering on others,
attached to the association of enmity, is not freed from suffering.

children.text: kuṇapassa pi gaṃdhucchijjati u 'ddhukitassa (-chitassa) pi rāti accayā |
children.translated_text: Even the smell of a corpse fades; even the scent of one who has been scorched disappears in time;

children.text: puruṣassa adhammacāriṇo annāhaṃ gandho na chijjati ||
children.translated_text: but for a man who practices <s>adharma</s>, the evil odor does not fade even in the other world.

children.text: yatha ggrahapatayo prabhūtaratanā āḍitte nagaramhi dahyamāne |
children.translated_text: Just as wealthy householders, when the city is ablaze and burning,
strive on account of their pearls, gems, crystals, and silver, [thinking] 'May we carry out something!'

children.text: tatha-r-iva śamaṇā prabhūtapraṃñā ayirā ayirapathesu sicchamānā |
children.translated_text: Just so, ascetics of great wisdom, noble ones training in the noble paths,

children.text: jātijarāmaraṇabhayāddittā dukkhāṭṭā vyāyamanti api prāpuṇema śāntiṃ ||
children.translated_text: ablaze with the fear of birth, old age, and death, afflicted by suffering, strive [thinking] 'May we attain peace!'

body.translated_text: <s>Kalyāṇīvarga</s> (The Chapter on the Virtuous) [ends].
***** <s>Puṣpa</s> (Flower) *****

children.text: na puṣpagandho paṭivātam eti na candanaṃ tagaraṃ vāhlikaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: The fragrance of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor that of sandalwood, <s>tagara</s>, or <s>vāhlika</s>;

children.text: satān tu gandho paṭivātam eti sabbā diśā sappuruṣo pravāti ||
children.translated_text: but the fragrance of the virtuous travels against the wind — the good person pervades all directions.

children.text: na puṣpagandhaḥ prativātam eti na vāhnijāt tagarāc candanād vā |
children.translated_text: The fragrance of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor that born of fire, nor from <s>tagara</s> or sandalwood;

children.text: satāṃ tu gandhaḥ prativātam eti sarvā diśaḥ satpuruṣaḥ pravāti ||
children.translated_text: but the fragrance of the virtuous travels against the wind — the good person pervades all directions.

children.text: candanaṃ tagaraṃ cāpi uppalaṃ atha vāśśikiṃ |
children.translated_text: Sandalwood, <s>tagara</s>, lotus, and also jasmine —
among all these types of fragrance, the fragrance of virtue is supreme.
Compared to <s>tagara</s>, sandalwood, jasmine, and likewise lotus —
among all these types of fragrance, the fragrance of virtue is indeed supreme.
Slight indeed is this fragrance that comes from <s>tagara</s> and sandalwood;

children.text: yo tu śīlavatāṃ gandho vāti devesu uttamo ||
children.translated_text: but the fragrance of the virtuous blows among the gods — it is supreme.

children.text: alpamātro hy ayaṃ gaṃdho yo 'yaṃ tagaracandanāt |
children.translated_text: Slight indeed is this fragrance that comes from <s>tagara</s> and sandalwood;

children.text: yas tu śīlavatāṃ gandho vāti deveṣv apīha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the fragrance of the virtuous blows even among the gods here.
Of those who are perfected in virtue, who dwell in heedfulness,
who are freed through perfect knowledge — <s>Māra</s> does not find their path.
Of those whose virtue is purified, who dwell in heedfulness,
who are freed through right knowledge — <s>Māra</s> does not find their path.

children.text: yathā pi ruciraṃ puṣpaṃ vannavantaṃ agandhakaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful flower that has color but no fragrance,

children.text: evaṃ subhāṣitā vācā aphalā hoti akurvvato ||
children.translated_text: so a well-spoken word is fruitless for one who does not act [upon it].

children.text: yathāpi ruciraṃ puṣpaṃ varṇavat syād agandhavat |
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful flower might have color but no fragrance,

children.text: evaṃ subhāṣitā vācā niṣphalā sāv akurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so a well-spoken word is fruitless for one who does not act [upon it].

children.text: yathā pi ruciraṃ puṣpaṃ vannavantaṃ sagaṃdhakaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful flower that has both color and fragrance,

children.text: evaṃ subhāṣitā vācā saphalā hoti kurvvato ||
children.translated_text: so a well-spoken word is fruitful for one who acts [upon it].

children.text: yathāpi ruciraṃ puṣpaṃ varṇavat syāt sugaṃdhavat |
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful flower that has both color and sweet fragrance,

children.text: evaṃ subhāṣitā vācā saphalā bhavati kurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so a well-spoken word becomes fruitful for one who acts [upon it].

children.text: yathā pi bhramaro puṣpā vannagandham aheḍayaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as a bee, without harming the color or fragrance of a flower,

children.text: praḍeti rasam ādāya evaṃ ggrāme munī care ||
children.translated_text: departs having taken the nectar — so should the sage go through the village.
Just as a bee, without harming the color or fragrance of a flower,

children.text: paraiti rasam ādāya tathā grāmaṃ muniś caret ||
children.translated_text: departs having taken the nectar — so should the sage go through the village.
The man who is merely gathering flowers, whose mind is attached —

children.text: suttaṃ ggrāmaṃ mahogho vā maccu-r-ādāya gacchati ||
children.translated_text: death carries him away, as a great flood [carries away] a sleeping village.
The man who is merely gathering flowers, whose mind is attached —

children.text: suptam grāmaṃ mahaughaiva mṛtyur ādāya gacchati ||
children.translated_text: death carries him away, just as a great flood [carries away] a sleeping village.
The man who is merely gathering flowers, whose mind is attached —
the Destroyer (Death) brings him under his power while his desires remain unfulfilled.
The man who is merely gathering flowers, whose mind is attached —

children.text: atṛptam eva kāmeṣu tv antakaḥ kurute vaśam ||
children.translated_text: the Destroyer (Death) brings him under his power while he is indeed unsated in desires.

body.text:
130 Dhp53
yathā pi puṣparāśimhā kayirā mālāguṇe bahū |
evaṃ jātena māccena kātavvaṃ kuśalaṃ bahuṃ |
Uv18:10
yathāpi puṣparāśibhyaḥ kuryān mālāguṇāṃ bahūn |
evaṃ jātena martyena kartavyaṃ kuśalaṃ bahu |
body.translated_text: 130 Dhp53 — Just as from a heap of flowers one might make many garlands, so by one born as a mortal, much good should be done. Uv18:10 — Just as from heaps of flowers one might make many garland-strings, so by one born a mortal, much good should be done.

children.text: ko imaṃ paṭhaviṃ vijehiti yamalokaṃ va imaṃ sadevakaṃ |
children.translated_text: Who shall conquer this earth, and this world of <s>Yama</s> together with the gods?

children.text: ko dhammapade sudeśite kuśalo puṣpam iva prajehiti ||
children.translated_text: Who, skilled, shall gather the well-taught verse of <s>Dharma</s>, as [one gathers] a flower?

children.text: ko imāṃ pṛthivīṃ vijeṣyte yamalokaṃ ca tathā sadevakam |
children.translated_text: Who shall conquer this earth, and likewise the world of <s>Yama</s> together with the gods?

children.text: ko dharmapadaṃ sudeśitaṃ kuśalaḥ puṣpam iva praceṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Who, skilled, shall gather the well-taught word of <s>Dharma</s>, as [one gathers] a flower?

children.text: śer̥̄kho paṭhaviṃ vijehiti yamalokaṃ va imaṃ sadevakaṃ |
children.translated_text: The learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) shall conquer this earth, and this world of <s>Yama</s> together with the gods;

children.text: so dhammapade sudeśite kuśalo puṣpam iva prajehiti ||
children.translated_text: he, skilled, shall gather the well-taught verse of <s>Dharma</s>, as [one gathers] a flower.

children.text: śaikṣaḥ pṛthivīṃ vijeṣyate yamalokaṃ va tathā sadevakam |
children.translated_text: The learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) shall conquer this earth, and likewise the world of <s>Yama</s> together with the gods;

children.text: sa hi dharmapadaṃ sudeśitaṃ kuśalo puṣpam iva prajehiti ||
children.translated_text: he indeed, skilled, shall gather the well-taught word of <s>Dharma</s>, as [one gathers] a flower.
Just as the jasmine sheds its withered flowers,

children.text: evaṃ rāgañ ca doṣañ ca vipramuñcatha bhikkhavo ||
children.translated_text: so should you, O <s>bhikkhus</s> (monks), cast off passion and hatred.

children.text: varṣāsu hi yathā puṣpaṃ vaguro vipramuñcati |
children.translated_text: Just as in the rains a shrub sheds its flowers,

children.text: evaṃ rāgaṃ ca doṣaṃ ca vipramuñcata bhikṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so should you, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), cast off passion and hatred.

children.text: phenopamaṃ lokam imaṃ vidittā marīcidhammaṃ abhisaṃbudhānāṃ |
children.translated_text: Having known this world to be like foam, having fully awakened to [its] mirage-nature,

children.text: chettāna mārassa prapuṣpakāni addaṃśanaṃ maccurājassa gacche ||
children.translated_text: having cut <s>Māra</s>'s flower-tipped [arrows], one should go beyond the sight of the King of Death.

children.text: phenopamaṃ kāyam imaṃ viditvā marīcidharmaṃ paribudhya caiva |
children.translated_text: Having known this body to be like foam, having fully awakened to [its] mirage-nature,

children.text: chitveha mārasya tu puṣpakāni tv adarśanaṃ mṛtyurājasya gacchet ||
children.translated_text: having cut <s>Māra</s>'s flower-[arrows] here, one should go beyond the sight of the King of Death.
Just as on a rubbish-heap cast upon the highway,
a lotus might spring up, pure-fragrant and delightful —
Just as on a rubbish-heap cast upon the highway,

children.text: padmaṃ tatra tu jāyeta śucigandhi manoramam ||
children.translated_text: a lotus might be born there, pure-fragrant and delightful —
so among people who have become like rubbish, among the spiritually blind common folk,
the disciples of the Perfectly Awakened One shine forth with wisdom.
So among these people who have become like rubbish, among the spiritually blind common folk,
the disciples of the Perfectly Awakened One shine forth with wisdom.

body.translated_text: <s>Puṣpavarga</s> (The Chapter on Flowers) [ends].
***** <s>Taṇhā</s> (Craving) *****

children.text: manujassa pramattacāriṇo tahnā vaddhati mālutā iva |
children.translated_text: For a man who lives heedlessly, craving grows like a creeping vine;

children.text: sā prāplavate hurāhuraṃ phalameṣī va vanamhi vānnaro ||
children.translated_text: he drifts from here to there, like a monkey in the forest seeking fruit.
Uv3:4

children.text: manujasya pramattacāriṇas tṛṣṇā vardhati māluteva hi |
children.translated_text: For a man who lives heedlessly, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) grows like a creeping vine indeed;

children.text: sa hi saṃsarate punaḥ punaḥ phalam icchann iva vānaro vane ||
children.translated_text: he wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> again and again, like a monkey in the forest desiring fruit.

children.text: yaṃ cesā sahate jaṃmī tahnā loke duraccayā |
children.translated_text: Whomsoever this wretched craving overcomes, so hard to escape in the world,

children.text: śokā tassa pravaddhaṃti ovaṭṭhā beruṇā iva ||
children.translated_text: sorrows increase for him, like <s>bīraṇa</s> grass after rain.
Uv3:9

children.text: ya etāṃ sahate grāmyāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ loke sudustyajām |
children.translated_text: Whomsoever endures this vulgar craving, so hard to abandon in the world,

children.text: śokās tasya pravardhante hy avavṛṣṭā bīraṇā yathā ||
children.translated_text: sorrows increase for him, like <s>bīraṇa</s> grass after rain.

children.text: yo cetāṃ sahate jaṃmiṃ tahnāṃ loke duraccayāṃ |
children.translated_text: But whoever overcomes this wretched craving, so hard to escape in the world,

children.text: śokā tassa vivaṭṭanti udabindū va pukkhare ||
children.translated_text: sorrows fall away from him, like a water drop from a lotus leaf.
