children.text: yas tv etāṃ tyajate grāmyāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ loke sudustyajām |
children.translated_text: But whoever abandons this vulgar craving, so hard to abandon in the world,

children.text: śokās tasya nivartante udabindur iva puṣkarāt ||
children.translated_text: sorrows turn away from him, like a water drop from a lotus.

children.text: taṃ vo vademi bhadraṃ vo yāvaṃt-ittha samāgatā |
children.translated_text: This I tell you — may it be well for you, all of you who have gathered here:

children.text: tahnāṃ samūlāṃ khaṇatha uṣīrātthī va beruṇiṃ |
children.translated_text: Dig up craving with its root, as one seeking fragrant <s>uśīra</s> [digs up] <s>bīraṇa</s> grass.

children.text: tahnāya khatamūlāya nāsti ṣokā kato bhayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: For one whose root of craving is dug up, there is no sorrow — whence fear?

children.text: tad vai vadāmi bhadraṃ vo yāvantaḥ stha samāgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: This indeed I tell you — may it be well for you, all of you who have gathered here:
Dig up craving with its root, as one seeking <s>uśīra</s> [digs up] <s>bīraṇa</s> grass.

children.text: tṛṣṇāyāḥ khātamūlāya nāsti ṣokaḥ kuto bhayam ||
children.translated_text: For one whose root of craving is dug up, there is no sorrow — whence fear?
A man with craving as his companion wanders through the long journey [of <s>saṃsāra</s>],
[taking] this form and that form, here and there, again and again.
A man with craving as his companion, through longing, [travels] the long road;
[taking] this form and that form, [he experiences] coming and going in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: etam ādīnavaṃ nyāttā tahnā dukkhassa saṃbhavaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having known this danger — that craving is the origin of suffering —
free from craving, without clinging, mindful, the <s>bhikkhu</s> (monk) should wander forth.

children.text: etad ādīnavaṃ jñātvā tṛṣṇā duḥkhasya saṃbhavaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having known this danger — that <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the origin of suffering —

children.text: vītatṛṣṇo hy anādānaḥ smṛto bhikṣuḥ parivrajet ||
children.translated_text: free from craving, without clinging, mindful, the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) should wander forth.

children.text: na taṃ dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam āhu dhīrā yad āyasaṃ dārujaṃ babbajaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: The wise do not call that bond strong which is made of iron, wood, or <s>babbaja</s> grass;

children.text: sārttarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu putresu dāresu ca yā apekhā ||
children.translated_text: [but rather] the passionate attachment to gems and earrings, and the longing for sons and wives.
Uv2:5

children.text: na tad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam āhur āryā yad āyasaṃ dāravaṃ balbajaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: The noble ones do not call that bond strong which is made of iron, wood, or <s>balbaja</s> grass;

children.text: saṃraktacittasya hi mandabuddheḥ putreṣu dāreṣu ca yā apekṣā ||
children.translated_text: [but rather] the longing of one whose mind is inflamed, who is dull-witted, for sons and wives.

children.text: etaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam āhu dhīrā ohārinaṃ sukhumaṃ dupramuñcaṃ |
children.translated_text: This [the wise] call a strong bond — dragging down, subtle, hard to release;

children.text: etappi chettāna vrajanti santo anapekhino sabbadukhaṃ prahāya ||
children.translated_text: having cut even this, the peaceful ones depart, without longing, having abandoned all suffering.
Uv2:6

children.text: etad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam āhur āryāḥ samantataḥ susthiraṃ duṣpramokṣam |
children.translated_text: This the noble ones call a strong bond — firm on all sides, difficult to free [oneself from];

children.text: etad api cchitvā tu parivrajanti hy anapekṣinaḥ kāmasukhaṃ prahāya ||
children.translated_text: having cut even this, they wander forth, without longing, having abandoned the pleasure of desires.

body.text:
145 Dhp186
na kāhāpaṇavāsena ttrettī kāmesu vijjati |

na karṣāpaṇavarṣeṇa tṛptiḥ kāmair hi vidyate |
body.translated_text: 145 Dhp186 — Not by a rain of gold coins is satisfaction found in sense-pleasures. Uv2:17 — Not by a rain of <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coins) is satisfaction found in desires.

body.text:
146 Dhp187
api divvesu kāmesu ratiṃ so nādhigacchati ||

body.translated_text: Even in divine pleasures, he does not find delight;

body.text:
Uv2:18
api divyeṣu kāmeṣu sa ratiṃ nādhigacchati ||
body.translated_text: the disciple of the Perfectly Awakened One delights in the destruction of craving.
Uv2:18 — Even in divine pleasures, he does not find delight; the disciple of the <s>Buddhas</s> always delights in the destruction of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving).

children.translated_text: Free from craving, without clinging, skilled in the etymologies of expressions,
knowing the grouping of syllables, their prior and subsequent [combinations] —

children.text: sa ve antimaśārīro mahapraṃño ti vuccati ||
children.translated_text: he is truly called one of 'last body,' of great wisdom.

children.text: saritāni sinehitāni ca somanassāni bhavanti jantuno |
children.translated_text: For a being, [there arise] flowing and clinging [attachments], and feelings of pleasure;

children.text: ye sātasitā sukheṣiṇo te ve jātijaropagā ||
children.translated_text: those who are attached to the agreeable, who seek happiness — they are subject to birth, old age, and [death].
Uv3:5

children.text: saritāni vai snehitāni vai saumanasyāni bhavanti jantunaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a being, [there arise] flowing and clinging [attachments], and feelings of pleasure;

children.text: ye sātasitāḥ sukhaiṣiṇas te vai jātijaropagā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those men who are attached to the agreeable, who seek happiness — they are subject to birth, old age, and [death].

children.text: tahnāya purekkhaṭā prajā parisappanti śaśo va bādhito |
children.translated_text: Driven by craving, people crawl about like a hare caught [in a snare];

children.text: te saṃjotanasaṅgasaṅgasattā gabbham upenti punappuno ciraṃ pi ||
children.translated_text: bound by fetters and attachments, they enter the womb again and again for a long time.
Uv3:6

children.text: tṛṣṇābhir upaskṛtāḥ prajāḥ paridhāvanti śaśā va vāgurām |
children.translated_text: Propelled by cravings, beings run about like a hare [running toward] a net;

children.text: saṃyojanaiḥ saṅgasaktā duḥkhaṃ yānti punaḥ punaś cirarātram ||
children.translated_text: bound by fetters and attachments, they go to suffering again and again for a long time.

children.text: muñca pure muñca pacchato majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū |
children.translated_text: Let go of the past, let go of the future, let go of the middle — gone beyond becoming;

children.text: sabbattha vimuttamānaso na puno jātijarām upehisi ||
children.translated_text: with mind released in every way, you will not again undergo birth and old age.

children.text: muñca purato muñca paścato madhye muñca bhavasya pāragaḥ |
children.translated_text: Let go of the front, let go of the behind, let go of the middle — gone beyond becoming;

children.text: sarvatra vimuktamānaso na punar jātijarām upeṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: with mind released in every way, you will not again undergo birth and old age.

children.text: yo nivvanadho vanā tu mutto vanamutto vanam eva dhāvati |
children.translated_text: One who, freed from the forest of desires, yet being released from that forest, runs back to the forest —

children.text: taṃ puggalam etha paśśatha mutto bandhanam eva dhāvati ||
children.translated_text: come, look at that person: once freed, he runs back to bondage.

children.text: yo nirvanagair vimokṣitaḥ saṃvanamukto vanam eva dhāvati |
children.translated_text: One who, liberated by those free from the forest of desires, released from the forest, runs back to the forest —

children.text: taṃ paśyatha pudgalaṃ tv imaṃ mukto bandhanam eva dhāvati ||
children.translated_text: behold that person: once freed, he runs back to bondage.
Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>rāga</s> (passion);

children.text: tassā hi vītarāgesu dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, what is given to those free from passion yields great fruit.

children.text: kṣetrāṇi tṛṇadoṣāṇi rāgadoṣā tv iyaṃ prajā |
children.translated_text: Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>rāga</s> (passion);
therefore, what is given to those free from passion yields great fruit.
Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred);

children.text: tassā hi vītadoṣesu dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, what is given to those free from hatred yields great fruit.

children.text: kṣetrāṇi tṛṇadoṣāṇi dveṣadoṣā tv iyaṃ prajā |
children.translated_text: Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred);

children.text: tasmād hi vigatadveṣebhyo dattaṃ bhavati mahāphalam ||
children.translated_text: therefore, what is given to those free from hatred yields great fruit.
Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>moha</s> (delusion);

children.text: tassā hi vītamohesu dinnaṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, what is given to those free from delusion yields great fruit.

children.text: kṣetrāṇi tṛṇadoṣāṇi mohadoṣā tv iyaṃ prajā |
children.translated_text: Fields have the blemish of weeds; this mankind has the blemish of <s>moha</s> (delusion);
therefore, what is given to those free from delusion yields great fruit.

children.text: ramaṇīyaṃ vatā 'raṇṇaṃ yamhiṃ na ramate jano |
children.translated_text: Delightful indeed are the forests where ordinary people find no delight;
those free from passion will delight there, for they are not seekers of sensual pleasures.

children.text: ramaṇīyāny araṇyāni na cātra ramate janaḥ |
children.translated_text: Delightful are the forests, yet ordinary people do not delight there;
those free from passion will delight there, but not those who seek sensual pleasures.

children.text: yathā pi mūle anupadrute dṛḍhe chinno pi rukkho puna-r-īva jāyati |
children.translated_text: Just as when the root is undamaged and firm, a tree though cut down grows again,

children.text: em eva tahnānuśaye anūhate nivvattate dukkham idaṃ punappuno ||
children.translated_text: even so, when the latent tendency of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is not uprooted, this <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) arises again and again.

children.text: yathāpi mūlair anupadrutaiḥ sadā chinno 'pi vṛkṣaḥ punar eva jāyate |
children.translated_text: Just as when the roots are always undamaged, a tree though cut down grows again,

children.text: evaṃ hi tṛṣṇānuśayair anuddhṛtair nirvartate duḥkham idaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even so, when the latent tendencies of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) are not uprooted, this <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) arises again and again.

body.translated_text: <s>taṇhāvargaḥ</s> (Chapter on Craving)
***** <s>Mala</s> (Impurity) *****

children.translated_text: Non-recitation is the impurity of the <s>Vedas</s>; non-exertion is the impurity of houses;

children.text: malo vaṇṇassa kosajjaṃ pramādo rakkhatāṃ malo ||
children.translated_text: laziness is the impurity of beauty; heedlessness is the impurity of a watchman.

children.text: malo istiye duccaritaṃ maccheraṃ dadatāṃ malo |
children.translated_text: Misconduct is the impurity of a woman; stinginess is the impurity of a giver;

children.text: malo pāpāni kaṃmāṇi assiṃ loke paramhi ca ||
children.translated_text: evil deeds are impurities both in this world and in the next.

children.text: tato malataraṃ brūmi avijjā maraṇaṃ malaṃ |
children.translated_text: But worse than these impurities, I declare: ignorance is the greatest impurity;
having abandoned these impurities, be stainless, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).

children.text: ayasā tu malo samuṭṭhito tato uṭṭhāya tam eva khādati |
children.translated_text: Just as rust arises from iron, and having arisen, eats that very iron,

children.text: em eva vidhūnacāriyaṃ sakāni kaṃmāṇi nayanti doggatiṃ ||
children.translated_text: even so, one's own <s>karmas</s> (deeds) lead the transgressor to a woeful state.

children.text: ayaso hi malaḥ samutthitaḥ sa tadutthāya tam eva khādati |
children.translated_text: Just as rust arises from iron, and having arisen, eats that very iron,

children.text: evam hy aniśāmyacāriṇaṃ svāni karmāṇi nayanti durgatim ||
children.translated_text: even so, one's own <s>karmas</s> (deeds) lead the heedless one to a woeful state.

children.text: pāṇḍupalāśo ca dāni si yamapuruṣā pi ca te upaṭṭhitā |
children.translated_text: You are now like a withered leaf, and <s>Yama's</s> messengers stand near you;

children.text: uyyogamukhe ca tiṣṭhasi pātheyaṃ pi ca te na vijjati ||
children.translated_text: you stand at the threshold of departure, yet you have no provision for the journey.

Strive, exert yourself, make an effort — as a smith purifies silver;
with impurities blown away, without blemish, you shall reach the celestial realm.

children.translated_text: Gradually, little by little, moment by moment,
the wise one should blow away one's own impurities, as a smith purifies silver.

children.text: anupūrveṇa medhāvī stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: Gradually, little by little, moment by moment,
the wise one should blow away one's own impurities, as a smith purifies silver.
Easy is the life of one without shame; he lives in a defiled manner,
bold, impudent, brave as a crow, boastful.
Easy would be life for one without shame, brave as a crow, acting like a raven,

children.text: praskandiṇā pragalbhena saṃkliṣṭaṃ tv iha jīvate ||
children.translated_text: bold and impudent — yet he lives in a defiled manner here.
But difficult is the life for one with a sense of shame, always seeking purity,
unattached, not impudent, living purely, seeing clearly.

children.text: hrīmatā tv iha durjīvaṃ nityaṃ śucigaveṣiṇā |
children.translated_text: But difficult is the life here for one with a sense of shame, always seeking purity,
well-restrained, not impudent, living purely, seeing clearly.

children.text: supaśśaṃ vajjaṃ aṃñesaṃ āttano puna duddaśaṃ |
children.translated_text: Easy to see are the faults of others, but one's own are difficult to see;

children.text: paresām iha vajjāni uppunāti yathā busaṃ |
children.translated_text: one winnows the faults of others like chaff,

children.text: āttano puna chādeti kalim va kṛtavāṃ śaṭho ||
children.translated_text: but conceals one's own, as a cheat conceals a losing throw.

children.text: supaśyaṃ paravadyaṃ syād ātmavadyaṃ tu durdṛśam |
children.translated_text: Easy to see would be the faults of others, but one's own faults are difficult to see;

children.text: paraḥ parasya vadyāni tūtpunāti busaṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: one winnows the faults of others like chaff,

children.text: ātmanaś chādayaty eṣa kṛtvā yadvat kaliṃ śaṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but conceals one's own, just as a cheat hides a losing throw.
Easy to do are things that are bad and harmful to oneself;

children.text: yaṃ ve hitaṃ ca sādhūni ca taṃ ve paramadukkharaṃ ||
children.translated_text: what is beneficial and good — that indeed is supremely difficult to do.

children.text: sukarāṇi hy asādhūni svātmano hy ahitāni ca |
children.translated_text: Easy to do are things that are bad and harmful to oneself;

children.text: yad vai hitaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca tad vai paramaduṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: what is beneficial and wholesome — that indeed is supremely difficult to do.
Easy to do are things that are bad and harmful to oneself;

children.text: yāni hitāni sādhūni tāni kurvvanti paṇḍitā ||
children.translated_text: those things that are beneficial and good — the wise do those.
They feel shame where there is nothing to be ashamed of, and feel no shame where shame is proper;
seeing danger where there is no danger, and seeing no danger where danger exists —
beings who hold wrong views go to a woeful state.
They feel shame where there is nothing to be ashamed of, and have no shame where shame is proper;
seeing danger where there is no danger, and seeing no danger where danger exists —
through holding <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong views), beings go to a woeful state.
Perceiving fault where there is no fault, and perceiving no fault where there is fault —
beings who hold wrong views go to a woeful state.
Those who think the unessential to be essential, and see the essential as unessential —
they do not attain the essential, being in the domain of wrong intentions.
Those who think the unessential to be essential, and perceive the essential as unessential —
they do not attain the essential, being in the domain of wrong intentions.

children.text: sārañ ca sārato ññāttā asārañ ca asārato |
children.translated_text: Having known the essential as essential, and the unessential as unessential —
they attain the essential, being in the domain of right intentions.

children.text: sāraṃ tu sārato jñātvā hy asāraṃ cāpi asārataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having known the essential as essential, and also the unessential as unessential —
they attain the essential, being in the domain of <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention).
Yoking oneself to what is not the proper practice, and not yoking oneself to the proper practice,
having abandoned the goal, grasping at what is pleasant, one envies those devoted to the true goal.
Uv5:9

children.text: avoge yujya cātmānaṃ yoge cāyujya sarvadā |
children.translated_text: Yoking oneself to what is not the proper practice, and always not yoking oneself to the proper practice,
having abandoned the goal, grasping at what is pleasant, one envies those devoted to the true goal.

body.translated_text: <s>malavargaḥ</s> (Chapter on Impurities)
***** <s>Bāla</s> (The Fool) *****

children.translated_text: Fools of little wisdom go about with the self as their own enemy,

children.text: karontā pāpakaṃ kammaṃ yaṃ hoti kaṭukapphalaṃ ||
children.translated_text: doing evil <s>karma</s> (deeds) that bear bitter fruit.

children.text: caranti bālā duṣprajñā hy amitrair iva cātmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Fools of poor wisdom go about with the self as their own enemy,

children.text: kurvantaḥ pāpakaṃ karma yad bhavati kaṭukaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: doing evil <s>karma</s> (deeds) that bear bitter fruit.

children.text: kathañ ca taṃ kare kaṃmaṃ yaṃ kattā anutappati |
children.translated_text: One should not do that deed which, having done, one repents,
the result of which one experiences weeping, with tears streaming down one's face.

children.text: na tat karrma kṛtaṃ sādhu yat kṛtvā hy anutapyate |
children.translated_text: That deed is not well done which, having done, one repents,
the result of which one experiences weeping, with tears streaming down one's face.

children.text: taṃ ca kaṃmaṃ kataṃ sādhu yaṃ kattā nānutappati |
children.translated_text: But that deed is well done which, having done, one does not repent,
the result of which one experiences joyfully, with a glad mind.

children.text: tat tu karma kṛtaṃ sādhu yat kṛtvā nānutapyate |
children.translated_text: But that deed is well done which, having done, one does not repent,
the result of which one experiences joyfully, with a glad mind.

children.text: yāvad eva anatthāya ñāttaṃ bālassa jāyati |
children.translated_text: Whatever knowledge arises for a fool, it is only to his detriment;

children.text: hanti bālassa śukrāṅggaṃ (?) muddham assa nipātaye ||
children.translated_text: it destroys the fool's bright portion and causes his head to fall.

children.text: yāvad eva hy anarthāya jñāto bhavati bāliśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Indeed, insofar as the fool becomes known, it is only to his detriment;

children.text: hanti bālasya śuklāṃśaṃ mūrdhāṃ cāsya pātayet ||
children.translated_text: it destroys the fool's bright portion and would cause his head to fall.

children.text: asatāṃ bhāvanam icchanti purekkhāñ ca bhikkhusu |
children.translated_text: The unworthy desire undeserved esteem, precedence among the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks),

children.text: āvāsesu ca essariyaṃ pūjaṃ parakulesu ca ||
children.translated_text: authority over the dwellings, and honor from other families.

children.text: asanto lābham icchanti satkāraṃ caiva bhikṣuṣu |
children.translated_text: The unworthy desire gain and honor among the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks),

children.text: āvāseṣu ca mātsaryaṃ pūjāṃ parakuleṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: possessiveness over the dwellings, and worship from other families.

children.text: mameva katamannentu gṛhī pravrajitā ca ye |
children.translated_text: "Let both householders and renunciants think that this was done by me alone;

children.text: na me pratibalā assa kiccā 'kiccesu kesuci ||
children.translated_text: let them be subject to my will in all matters, whether duties or not" —

children.text: mām eva nityaṃ jānīyur gṛhī pravrajitas tathā |
children.translated_text: "Let both householders and renunciants always know me alone;

children.text: mama prativaśāś ca syuḥ kṛtyākṛtyeṣu keṣu cit ||
children.translated_text: let them be subject to my will in all matters, whether duties or not" —
180 Dhp74ef,75ab

children.text: iti bālassa saṃkappo icchāmāno ca vaddhati |
children.translated_text: such is the intention of a fool, and his desire and pride increase;
for one is the path to worldly gain, and another is the path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Such are the intentions of a fool — they increase desire and craving;
for one is the basis for worldly gain, and another is the path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
181 Dhp75c-f

children.text: evam etaṃ yathābhūtaṃ paśśaṃ buddhassa sāvako |
children.translated_text: Thus understanding this as it truly is, the disciple of the <s>Buddha</s>
should not delight in worldly honor, but should cultivate seclusion.

children.text: etaj jñātvā yathābhūtaṃ buddhānāṃ śrāvakaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Having known this as it truly is, the disciple of the <s>Buddhas</s> should always
not delight in worldly honor, but should cultivate seclusion.

children.text: jayaṃ ve manyate bālo vācāya paruṣaṃ bhaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: The fool thinks he is winning when speaking harsh words;

children.text: satāṃ hesa jayo hoti yā titikkhā vijānato ||
children.translated_text: but true victory belongs to the good, which is the patient endurance of one who understands.

children.text: jayaṃ hi manyate bālo vacobhiḥ paruṣair vadan |
children.translated_text: The fool thinks he is winning when speaking harsh words;

children.text: nityam iva jayas tasya yo 'tivākhaṃ titīkṣati ||
children.translated_text: but victory is always his who endures abuse with patience.

children.text: abalaṃ tassa balaṃ hoti yassa bālabalaṃ balaṃ |
children.translated_text: The strength of one whose strength is the strength of a fool is really no strength;
for one who is guarded by <s>dharma</s>, no adversary can be found.

children.text: abalaṃ hi balaṃ tasya yasya krodhe balaṃ balam |
children.translated_text: The strength of one whose strength lies in anger is really no strength;
for one who is angry and devoid of <s>dharma</s>, there is no right course of action.

children.text: yo bālo bālamānī paṇḍito cāpi tattha so |
children.translated_text: A fool who knows he is a fool is wise at least in that;

children.text: bālo tu paṇḍitamānī sa ve bālo ti vuccati ||
children.translated_text: but a fool who thinks himself wise — he is truly called a fool.

children.text: yo jānīyād ahaṃ bāla iti bālaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A fool who knows "I am a fool" — that fool is wise;

children.text: bālaḥ paṇḍitamānī tu bāla eva nirucyate ||
children.translated_text: but a fool who thinks himself wise is truly called a fool.

children.text: drīghā assupato rātrī drīghaṃ śāntassa yojanaṃ |
children.translated_text: Long is the night for the sleepless; long is the <s>yojana</s> (league) for the weary;
long is <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) for fools who do not know the true <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dīrghā jāgarato rātrir dīrghaṃ śrāntasya yojanam |
children.translated_text: Long is the night for the wakeful; long is the <s>yojana</s> (league) for the weary;
long is <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) for the fool who does not know the true <s>dharma</s>.
If a man wraps a rotten fish in <s>kuśa</s> grass,

children.text: kuśā pi pūtiṃ vāyanti evaṃ bālopasevanā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kuśa</s> grass too will smell foul — such is the association with fools.

children.text: pūtimatsyāṃ kuśāgreṇa yo naro hy upanahyate |
children.translated_text: If a man wraps a rotten fish in <s>kuśa</s> grass,

children.text: kuśāpi pūtikā vānti hy evaṃ pāpopasevanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kuśa</s> grass too will smell foul — such is the association with the wicked.

children.text: tagarañ ca palāśamhi yo naro upanahyati |
children.translated_text: If a man wraps <s>tagara</s> (fragrant powder) in a leaf,

children.text: pattaṃ pi surabhiṃ vāti evaṃ dhīropasevanā ||
children.translated_text: the leaf too will smell sweet — such is the association with the wise.

children.text: tagaraṃ palāśapatreṇa yo naro hy upanahyati |
children.translated_text: If a man wraps <s>tagara</s> (fragrant powder) in a leaf,

children.text: patrāṇy api sugandhīni sad evaṃ saṃgamāt satām ||
children.translated_text: even the leaves become fragrant — such is the result of associating with the good.

children.text: akaronto pi ce pāpaṃ karonte upasevati |
children.translated_text: Even if one does no evil oneself, if one associates with those who do,

children.text: śaṅkiyo hoti pāpamhi avaṇṇo cāssa rūhati ||
children.translated_text: one becomes suspected of evil, and ill repute grows for him.
Even if one does no evil deeds, if one associates with those who do,

children.text: śaṅkito bhavati pāpasya avarṇaś cāsya vardhate ||
children.translated_text: one becomes suspected of evil, and ill repute grows for him.
One who associates with those who associate with evil, touched by those who touch others —

children.text: śaro litto kalāpe vā alitte upaliṃpati |
children.translated_text: like a poisoned arrow in a quiver that smears the unpoisoned ones,
fearing such contamination, the wise one should never be a friend of the wicked.

children.text: saṃsevamānaḥ pāpo hi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ saṃsphṛśet parān |
children.translated_text: For evil, associating with others, being touched, touches others in turn;
a poisoned arrow in a quiver smears the unpoisoned ones,
fearing such contamination, the wise one should never be a friend of the wicked.
Like a fruit-basket, one should know one's own ripening;
the wise one should not associate with the bad, but should associate with the good.
Therefore, as with a basket of fruit, having seen one's own ripening,
the wise one should not associate with the bad, but should associate with the good.

children.text: yāvaj jīvaṃ pi ce bālo paṇḍite payirupāsati |
children.translated_text: Even if a fool attends upon a wise person for his whole life,

children.text: neva dhammaṃ vijānāti dravvī sūparasān iva ||
children.translated_text: he does not understand the <s>Dharma</s>, just as a ladle [does not know] the taste of soup.

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ pi ced bālaḥ paṇḍitāṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Even if a fool attends upon the wise for his whole life,

children.text: na sa dharmaṃ vijānāti darvī sūparasān iva ||
children.translated_text: he does not understand the <s>Dharma</s>, just as a ladle [does not know] the taste of soup.

children.text: muhuttam api ce praṃño paṇḍite payirupāsati |
children.translated_text: But if a wise person attends upon the wise even for a moment,

children.text: khipraṃ dhammaṃ vijānāti jihvā sūparasān iva ||
children.translated_text: he quickly understands the <s>Dharma</s>, just as the tongue [knows] the taste of soup.
Even for a moment, a wise person attends upon the wise;

children.text: sa vai dharmaṃ vijānāti jihvā sūparasān iva ||
children.translated_text: he truly understands the <s>Dharma</s>, just as the tongue [knows] the taste of soup.

children.text: nāppaṃ pāpassa maṃñeyā na me taṃ āgamiṣyati |
children.translated_text: One should not think lightly of evil, [saying] 'It will not come to me';
by the falling of water drops, even a water pot is filled;

body.text: pūrate bālo pāpassa thokathokaṃ pi ācinaṃ |

children.text: nālpaṃ manyeta pāpasya naitaṃ mām āgamiṣyati |

by the falling of water drops, even a great vessel is filled;

children.translated_text: fools are filled with evils, even those done little by little.

***** <s>Daṇḍa</s> (Punishment) *****

children.text: na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṃko nānāśanaṃ tthaṇḍīlaśāyikā vā |
children.translated_text: Neither going naked, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting, nor sleeping on the ground,
nor dust and dirt, nor squatting austerities can purify a mortal who has not overcome doubt.

children.text: na nagacaryā na jaṭā na paṅkā no 'nāśanaṃ sthaṇḍīlaśāyikā vā |
children.translated_text: Neither going naked, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting, nor sleeping on the ground,

children.text: na rajomalaṃ notkuṭukaprahāṇaṃ śodheta martyaṃ hy avitīrṇakāṅkṣaṃ ||
children.translated_text: nor dust and dirt, nor squatting austerities can purify a mortal who has not overcome doubt.

children.text: alaṃkato cāpi samaṃ careyā dānto śānto niyato dhammacārī |
children.translated_text: Even if adorned, one should live peacefully — restrained, calm, disciplined, living by <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sabbesu prāṇesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ so brāhmaṇo so śamaṇo sa bhikkhū ||
children.translated_text: having laid down the rod toward all living beings — he is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he is a <s>Śramaṇa</s>, he is a <s>Bhikṣu</s>.

children.text: alaṃkṛtaś cāpi careta dgarmaṃ kṣānto dānto niyato brahmacārī |
children.translated_text: Even if adorned, one should practice the <s>Dharma</s> — patient, restrained, disciplined, living the holy life,

children.text: sarveṣu bhūteṣu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ sa brāhmaṇaḥ sa śramaṇaḥ sa bhikṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: having laid down the rod toward all beings — he is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he is a <s>Śramaṇa</s>, he is a <s>Bhikṣu</s>.

children.text: mā vade paruṣaṃ kaṃci vuttā paṭivadeyu taṃ |
children.translated_text: Do not speak harshly to anyone; those spoken to would answer you back;

children.text: dukkhā hi sārambhakathā paṭidaṇḍā phuseyu taṃ ||
children.translated_text: painful indeed is contentious speech; retaliatory blows would reach you.

children.text: mā kaṃ cit paruṣaṃ brūthaḥ proktāḥ prativadanti tam |
children.translated_text: Do not speak harshly to anyone; those spoken to answer back;

children.text: duḥkhā hi saṃrambhakathāḥ pratidaṇḍaṃ spṛśanti hi ||
children.translated_text: painful indeed are contentious words; retaliatory blows reach [the speaker].
If you make yourself resound like a struck gong,
you will experience the cycle of birth and death (<s>saṃsāra</s>) for a long time.
If you make yourself resound like a gong that is always struck,
you will experience the cycle of birth and death (<s>saṃsāra</s>) for a long time.

children.text: na ce iresi āttānaṃ kaṃso anupahato-r-iva |
children.translated_text: But if you do not make yourself resound, like an unstruck gong,

children.text: esa prātto si nibbāṇaṃ sārambhā te na vijjati ||
children.translated_text: you have attained <s>Nibbāna</s> (extinction); there is no contentiousness in you.

children.text: na tv īrayasi hātmānaṃ kaṃsir nopahatā yathā |
children.translated_text: But if you do not make yourself resound, like a gong that is not struck,

children.text: eṣa prāpto 'si nirvāṇaṃ saṃrambhas te na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: you have attained <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; there is no contentiousness in you.

children.text: evaṃ jarā ca maccū ca prāṇināṃ adhivattati ||
children.translated_text: so old age and death drive the life of living beings onward.

children.text: yathā daṇḍena gopālo gāḥ prāpayati gocaram |

children.text: evaṃ rogair jarāmṛtyuḥ āyuḥ prāpayate nṛṇām ||

children.text: āttānaṃ upamaṃ kattā neva haṃyyā na ghātaye ||

children.text: ātmānam upamāṃ kṛtvā naiva hanyān na ghātayet ||

children.text: āttano sukham eṣāṇo precca so na labhate sukhaṃ ||
children.translated_text: seeking happiness for himself, does not obtain happiness after death.

children.text: na bhajetha pāpake mitre na bhajetha puruṣā 'dhame |
children.translated_text: One should not associate with evil friends, nor associate with the lowest of men;
the wise and intelligent one should associate with the best of men;

children.text: tārise bhajemānassa śreyo hoti na pāpiyo ||
children.translated_text: for one who associates with such, there is betterment, not evil.

children.text: na bhajet pāpakaṃ mitraṃ na bhajet puruṣādhamam |
children.translated_text: One should not associate with an evil friend, nor associate with the lowest of men;
one should associate with a good friend, one should associate with the best of men;

children.text: tādṛśaṃ bhajamānasya śreyo bhavati na pāpakam ||
children.translated_text: for one who associates with such, there is betterment, not evil.

children.text: nidhino va pravattāraṃ yaṃ paśśe vajjadaṃśinaṃ |
children.translated_text: Should one find a person who points out faults, like one who reveals a treasure,
a wise critic — one should associate with such a person;

children.text: tāriṣaṃ bhajamānassa śreyo hoti na pāpiyo ||
children.translated_text: for one who associates with such, there is betterment, not evil.
One who prohibits, who speaks out, whom one should know as a fault-seer,
a wise critic — one should always associate with such;

children.text: tādṛśaṃ bhajamānasya śreyo bhavati na pāpakam ||
children.translated_text: for one who associates with such, there is betterment, not evil.
Let him admonish, let him instruct, let him restrain from the improper;

children.text: satāṃ hetaṃ priyaṃ hoti asatāṃ hoti apriyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: he becomes dear to the good; he becomes unpleasant to the bad.
Let him admonish, instruct, and restrain from the improper;

children.text: asatāṃ na priyo bhavati satāṃ bhavati priyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: he does not become dear to the bad; he becomes dear to the good.

children.text: tassā satāñ ca asantāñ ca nānā hoti gatī |
children.translated_text: Therefore the good and the bad have different destinations;
the bad go to hell; the good are bound for heaven.

children.text: asantaś caiva santaś ca nānā yānti tv itaś cyutāḥ |
children.translated_text: The bad and the good, having departed from here, go to different places;
the bad go to hell; the good are bound for heaven.
This person of little learning ages like an ox;

children.text: māṃsāni tassa vaddhanti praṃñā tassa na vaddhanti ||
children.translated_text: his flesh increases, but his wisdom does not increase.

children.text: cattāri ṭṭhāṇāni naro pramatto āpajjate paradāropasevī |
children.translated_text: Four states the heedless man incurs who is a pursuer of others' wives:

children.text: apuṃñalābhaṃ anikāmaśeyaṃ nindaṃ tritīyaṃ nirayaṃ catutthaṃ ||
children.translated_text: acquisition of demerit, uncomfortable sleep, blame as the third, and hell as the fourth.

children.text: sthānāni catvāri naraḥ pramatta āpadyate yaḥ paradārasevī |
children.translated_text: Four states the heedless man incurs who is a pursuer of others' wives:

children.text: apunyalābhaṃ hy anikāmaśayyaṃ nindāṃ tṛtīyaṃ narakaṃ caturtham ||
children.translated_text: acquisition of demerit, uncomfortable sleep, blame as the third, and hell as the fourth.

children.text: apuṃñalābho ca gatī ca pāpiko bhītassa bhītāya ratī pi appikā |
children.translated_text: Acquisition of demerit and an evil destination; the pleasure of a frightened man with a frightened woman is brief;

children.text: rājā pi daṇḍaṃ garukaṃ praṇeti kāyassa bhedā nirayaṃ upeti ||
children.translated_text: the king imposes heavy punishment; upon the breaking up of the body, he goes to hell.

children.text: apuṇyalābhaṃ ca gatiṃ ca pāpikāṃ bhītasya bhītābhir athālpikāṃ ratim |
children.translated_text: Acquisition of demerit and an evil destination; the pleasure of a frightened man with a frightened woman is brief;

children.text: rājā ca daṇḍaṃ garukaṃ dadāti kāyasya bhedād narakeṣu pacyate ||
children.translated_text: the king gives heavy punishment; upon the breaking up of the body, he is cooked in the hells.

children.text: saṃyyatā sugatiṃ yānti doggatiṃ yānti asaṃyyātā |
children.translated_text: The restrained go to a good destination; the unrestrained go to a bad destination;

children.text: mā ssu viśśāsam āpādi iti vindu samaṃ care ||
children.translated_text: do not fall into carelessness — knowing this, practice equanimity.

children.text: mākuñjara nāgam āsida dukkho kuñjara nāgamaṃsado |
children.translated_text: Do not approach the great elephant, O elephant! Painful is he who feeds on elephant flesh;

children.text: na hi nāgahatassa kuñjara sugatī ito paraaṃ yato ||
children.translated_text: for one who has slain an elephant, O elephant, there is no good destination hereafter.
Just as a lion roaming in mountain strongholds, grazing in mountain pastures,
a hero among men, fearless — do not harm [him] of extraordinary stride.

children.text: ahaṃ nāgo va saṃggrāme cāpātipatite śare |
children.translated_text: I, like an elephant in battle, endure arrows shot from bows;
I shall endure harsh speech, for many people are of bad character.

children.text: ahaṃ nāga iva saṃgrāme cāpād utpatitāṃ śarān |
children.translated_text: I, like an elephant in battle, [endure] arrows shot from bows;
I shall endure harsh words, for the multitude is of bad character.

children.text: bahū ve śaraṇaṃ yānti parvvate ca vanāni ca |
children.translated_text: Many go for refuge to mountains and forests,
to shrines, sacred trees, and groves — people struck by fear.

children.text: bahavaḥ śaraṇaṃ yānti parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca |
children.translated_text: Many go for refuge to mountains and forests,
to parks and tree-shrines — people struck by fear.

children.text: na etaṃ śaraṇaṃ khemmaṃ na etaṃ śaraṇaṃ uttamaṃ |
children.translated_text: This is not a safe refuge; this is not the supreme refuge;
by coming to this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.

children.text: naitad dhi śaraṇaṃ kṣemaṃ naitac charaṇaṃ uttamam |
children.translated_text: This is not a safe refuge; this is not the supreme refuge;
by coming to this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.

children.text: yo tu buddhañ ca dhammañ ca saghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gato |
children.translated_text: But he who has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>,
and sees as they truly are the Four Noble Truths (<s>Āryasatyas</s>) —

children.text: yas tu buddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>,
and when he sees with wisdom the Four Noble Truths (<s>Āryasatyas</s>) —

children.text: etaṃ ve śaraṇaṃ khemmaṃ etaṃ śaraṇam uttamaṃ |
children.translated_text: This is indeed a safe refuge; this is the supreme refuge;
by coming to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.

children.text: etad dhi śaraṇaṃ kṣemam etac charaṇam uttamam |
children.translated_text: This is indeed a safe refuge; this is the supreme refuge;
by coming to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.

children.text: gavāṃ ce taramāṇānāṃ jihmaṃ gacchati puṅgavo |
children.translated_text: If, among cattle crossing [a river], the bull goes crookedly,

children.text: sabbā tā jihmaṃ gacchaṃti nette jihmagate sati ||
children.translated_text: all of them go crookedly, when the leader has gone astray.

children.text: evām eva manuṣyesu yo hoti śreṣṭhasaṃmato |
children.translated_text: Even so among humans, he who is considered the best,

children.text: sa ce adhaṃmaṃ carati prāg eva itarā prajā ||
children.translated_text: if he practices <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) — how much more so the rest of the people!

children.text: gavāṃ ce taramāṇānāṃ ujjuṃ gacchati puṅgavo |
children.translated_text: If, among cattle crossing [a river], the bull goes straight,

children.text: sabbā tā ujjuṃ gacchaṃti nette ujjugate sati ||
children.translated_text: all of them go straight, when the leader has gone straight.

children.text: evām eva manuṣyesu yo hoti śreṣṭhasaṃmato |
children.translated_text: Even so among humans, he who is considered the best,

children.text: sa ce dhaṃmaṃ carati prāg eva itarā prajā ||
children.translated_text: if he practices <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) — how much more so the rest of the people!

children.translated_text: One should practice the <s>Dharma</s> well; one should not practice it badly;

children.text: dhammacārī sukhaṃ śeti assiṃ loke paramhi ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner sleeps happily, in this world and in the next.

children.text: dharmaṃ caret sucaritaṃ nainaṃ duścaritaṃ caret |
children.translated_text: One should practice the <s>Dharma</s> well; one should not practice it badly;

children.text: dharmacārī sukhaṃ śete hy asmiṃ loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner sleeps happily, in this world and in the next.

children.text: dhaṃmaṃ care sucaritaṃ na naṃ duccaritaṃ care |
children.translated_text: One should practice the <s>Dharma</s> well; one should not practice it badly;

children.text: brahmacārī sukhaṃ śeti assiṃ loke paramhi ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Brahmacārī</s> (celibate practitioner) sleeps happily, in this world and in the next.
Delighting in <s>Dharma</s>, rejoicing in <s>Dharma</s>, contemplating the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: dhammam anussaraṃ bhikkhū dhammā na parihāyati ||
children.translated_text: recollecting the <s>Dharma</s>, a <s>Bhikkhu</s> does not fall away from the <s>Dharma</s>.
Delighting in <s>Dharma</s>, rejoicing in <s>Dharma</s>, contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> alone,

children.text: dharmaṃ cānusmaraṃ bhikṣur dharmān na parihīyate ||
children.translated_text: and recollecting the <s>Dharma</s>, a <s>Bhikṣu</s> does not fall away from the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> indeed protects the <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner; <s>Dharma</s> well-practiced brings happiness;

children.translated_text: this is the benefit of <s>Dharma</s> well-practiced — the <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner does not go to a bad destination.

children.text: ekāhaṃ jīvitaṃ śreyaḥ paśyato hy amṛtaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: better is a single day's life of one who sees the deathless state.

children.text: yo ca vaśśaśataṃ jīve saddhaṃme apratiṣṭhito |

children.text: ekā 'haṃ jīvitaṃ śreyo sadhaṃmaṃ iha vijānato ||
children.translated_text: better is a single day's life of one who understands the true <s>Dharma</s> here.

children.text: yo ca vaśśaśataṃ jīve aprāpya āsavakkhayaṃ |
children.translated_text: Though one should live a hundred years, not attaining the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (mental influxes),

children.text: yac ca varṣaśataṃ jīved apaśyann āsravakṣayam |

children.translated_text: He for whom there are no thickets of desire whatsoever, binding one to existence and causing [rebirth],

children.translated_text: that <s>Bhikkhu</s> (monk) abandons this shore and the far shore, as a serpent [sheds] its old worn-out skin.

children.translated_text: He for whom there are no thickets of desire whatsoever, and whose root of the unwholesome is destroyed,

children.translated_text: that <s>Bhikṣu</s> (monk) abandons this [world] and the far shore, as a serpent [sheds] its old worn-out skin.

children.translated_text: He for whom there are no thickets of desire whatsoever, whose roots of the unwholesome have been uprooted,

children.translated_text: that <s>Bhikkhu</s> (monk) abandons this shore and the far shore, as a serpent [sheds] its old worn-out skin.

body.text: samāptā dhammapadā amṛtapadāni gāthāśatāni pañca dve ca gāthe || yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitam iti parihāroyam asmadīyaḥ || śubhaṃ astu sarvvasatvānānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmapadā</s> is completed: five hundred and two verses of deathless utterances. As it was seen, so it was written — this is our disclaimer. May there be well-being for all beings.
